# arioso

Unified Python facade for AI music generation.

One interface, many backends. Arioso wraps 16 AI music generation platforms —
from local open-source models to commercial REST APIs — behind a single `generate()` call.

## Install

```default
pip install arioso
```

## Quick start

```python
import arioso

# Generate music (defaults to MusicGen, runs locally)
song = arioso.generate("upbeat jazz piano")

# The result is a Song object with audio data
song.audio.audio_array  # numpy array (for local models)
song.audio.sample_rate  # e.g. 32000

# Use a different platform
song = arioso.generate("epic orchestral soundtrack", platform="elevenlabs", duration=30)
song.audio.audio_bytes  # MP3 bytes
```

## Command line

Installing arioso also installs an `arioso` command (`python -m arioso` does the same).

```default
arioso generate "warm lo-fi piano" --platform musicgen --duration 10 -o out.wav
arioso generate "ambient pads" --platform stable_audio --model stabilityai/stable-audio-open-1.0 --seed 7 -o pads.wav
arioso platforms
```

`generate` writes the audio and prints the path it wrote. A waveform from a local model is written as WAV (with `soundfile` when installed, else the standard library’s `wave`); encoded audio from a hosted platform keeps its format, and the file’s suffix follows it. `--model` and `--seed` are passed on only when given.

`platforms` lists every platform with its access type, weights licence and whether its output may be used commercially (`yes`, `no`, `conditional`, `unclear` when the terms are not settled (licence unstated, disputed or withdrawn, or a doubtful training-data chain), or `provider terms` for hosted models whose service terms decide). The same table is `arioso.platform_table()` in Python, and each platform’s `weights_license` and `commercial_use` are in `arioso.get_platform_info(name)`. MusicGen’s weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0, so its output is not for commercial use.

Local torch platforms (MusicGen on transformers, Stable Audio Open) run on CUDA, else Apple MPS, else CPU; set `ARIOSO_TORCH_DEVICE` to force one.

### Comparing platforms

`compare` renders the same prompts with several platforms and measures each take:

```default
arioso compare stable_audio_3,magenta_rt,ace_step:runtime=local --prompts prompts.json --duration 10
```

A contender is a platform with optional `key=value` options (`musicgen:model=facebook/musicgen-small`). Each one runs in a fresh process, one after the other, so only one model is in memory at a time and its peak memory is its own: on macOS the peak physical footprint, which counts Metal allocations, on Linux the peak resident set, in GB (10^9 bytes), for the process and, sampled while it runs, for the processes it starts (a runtime’s worker, or one process per take). Every take becomes one JSON line in `<out_dir>/results.jsonl`: model load plus warm-up time, generation time, real-time factor (generation time over the seconds that came back), peak memory, available memory before the run, the weights licence, and objective checks: peak level and clipping (takes are kept as float WAVs, so a peak over full scale shows), and, when `denote` is installed, the detected tempo against the prompt’s `bpm` (half and double time forgiven) and the estimated key against its `key`. A check that cannot run says why under `checks_skipped`. Takes of one run go to `<out_dir>/<run id>/<contender>/<prompt id>.wav` with a page of players beside them (`index.html`), and the command prints a progress line per take, then a summary per contender.

Load times compare like with like only between runtimes of the same kind: a runtime that keeps a worker (Magenta RealTime, ACE-Step) loads once, in the warm-up, while one that starts a process per take (Stable Audio 3) loads in every take, so its load is inside its real-time factor.

Without `--prompts` it uses three built-in prompts (a groove at 100 BPM, an accompaniment in C major, a loop at 85 BPM). A prompts file is a JSON list of `{"id", "text", "bpm", "key", "melody", "duration"}` (only `text` is required; a `melody` path is passed to platforms that take one). Platforms that may call a paid hosted service are refused unless you pass `--allow-hosted`: anything that is not a `python_lib` or `local_runtime`, has provider terms, or takes any credential (even an optional one, as `yue` takes a fal key); `runtime=local` counts as local only on a platform that has a local runtime (`ace_step`). `--min-free-gb` skips a contender when the machine is short of memory.

In Python, `arioso.compare.compare(contenders, prompts)` yields the same records. Its seams are `runner=` (how a contender is run and measured: `in_child_process`, with `python=`, or `in_this_process`), `scorer=` (audio to a dict of checks), `preload=` (modules that register third-party platforms, run here and in each child; `--preload` on the command line) and `timeout=` (seconds before a contender is killed with every process it started; `--timeout`). A killed or crashing contender keeps the takes it finished. Worker memory is sampled every 0.1 s, so it is a lower bound: memory a process takes just before exiting can be missed.

## Enhance existing audio (audio-to-audio)

Beyond text-to-music, arioso can transform audio you already have – e.g. turn a
plain synthesized/”MIDI” render into something richer, or re-generate music that
follows an input melody. This is the `enhance()` entry point:

```python
import arioso

rendered = (
    ...
)  # a Song, a file path, bytes, an (array, sample_rate) pair, or a numpy waveform

# Audio-to-audio: continue/transform the input (Stable Audio Open, local)
better = arioso.enhance(rendered, "warm analog studio band", platform="stable_audio")

# Subtle variation: low strength keeps the input, high lets the prompt take over
# (Stable Audio 2.5 on fal.ai; needs FAL_KEY)
close = arioso.enhance(
    rendered, "full symphony orchestra", platform="stable_audio_25", strength=0.3
)

# Remix toward style tags (ACE-Step on fal.ai)
remix = arioso.enhance(rendered, "orchestral, film score, brass", platform="ace_step")

# Melody-conditioned: keep the tune, take the style from the prompt (MusicGen-melody)
variation = arioso.enhance(rendered, "energetic EDM", platform="musicgen")

# Discover which platforms accept input audio
arioso.supports_audio_input("stable_audio")  # True
arioso.supports_audio_input("mubert")  # False
```

To *extend* a recording rather than transform it, pass it as `continue_from` to `musicgen`. The last `prompt_seconds` (default 10) of the audio prompt the model, which writes `extend_seconds` (default `duration`) of what comes next, chained over `rounds` calls. The result is the original followed by the continuation; the continuation alone is in `song.metadata["continuation"]`. It runs locally, so it also extends audio that a hosted extend route refuses (Suno’s `upload_extend` rejects uploads that match a catalogued composition).

```python
longer = arioso.generate(
    "warm piano trio",
    platform="musicgen",
    model="facebook/musicgen-medium",
    continue_from="take.wav",
    prompt_seconds=10,
    extend_seconds=20,
    rounds=2,
)
```

`enhance(audio, prompt='', *, platform='stable_audio', strength=None, as_='auto')`
routes your audio into the platform’s audio-conditioning affordance
(`audio_input`, `melody`, or `reference_audio`) and generates. Input audio is
accepted in any form a `Song`/`AudioResult`/`bytes`/path/`(array, sample_rate)`/
numpy-waveform can take (normalized internally). Note that `stable_audio` via
diffusers uses the input as an initial waveform (continuation/init) and has no
`strength` knob (a value passed there is ignored with a warning); for a
strength-controlled transform use `stable_audio_25`.

## Seeds: a melody over a drone

To make a generator keep a known melody with no harmony (a Suno upload-cover, MusicGen-melody), give it the melody alone over a drone: a cover keeps its source’s harmony static, so a source with no harmony gives takes that hold the drone. `arioso.seeds` builds that source from a recording or a score (`pip install 'arioso[seeds]'`; separating a voice from a mix goes through `denote`, which also needs `torch` and `torchaudio`).

```python
from arioso.seeds import melody_contour, melody_over_drone
from arioso.analysis import drone_report, melody_match

contour = melody_contour(
    "song.mid"
)  # one MIDI track's skyline, with glides and vibrato
contour = melody_contour(
    "song.mp3"
)  # or a recording: voice separated, f0 tracked, cleaned
seed, sr = melody_over_drone(
    contour.transposed(-3), "C#"
)  # bowed line over a tanpura on C#

drone_report(take, sr, sa="C#").holds()  # does a take hold the drone?
melody_match(take, seed, sr)  # does it keep the tune? (~0.9 vs ~0.45 for another song)
```

Every step is a seam: `audio_contour(..., separator=, f0_tracker=)`, `melody_over_drone(..., drone=, timbre=)`. A low (male) line is lifted by octaves above the drone’s register (`floor_midi`), where it would otherwise fail `drone_report`.

A real tanpura sounds less synthetic than `tanpura()`: pass a recording as `drone=` (or `drone=recorded_drone(y, sr)`). It is retuned to Sa by varispeed (up to `max_shift`, 2 semitones by default) and looped with crossfades. A CC0 one to start from: [“Tanpura in E”](https://freesound.org/s/148850/) on Freesound.

For a source in a generator’s own phrasing, `musicgen_variation(voice, "C#", prompt="slow sarangi", transpose=..., slow=1.2)` runs MusicGen-melody on the voice over the drone, high-passes its take below the drone’s band, and puts the drone back underneath.

19 platforms are included, spanning local models, REST APIs, and SDK-based services:

| **MusicGen**               | Local (audiocraft/transformers)                   | None                                 | `pip install arioso[musicgen]`        |
| **Stable Audio Open**      | Local (diffusers)                                 | None                                 | `pip install arioso[stable-audio]`    |
| **Harmonai**               | Local (diffusers)                                 | None                                 | `pip install arioso[harmonai]`        |
| **Riffusion**              | Local (diffusers)                                 | None                                 | `pip install arioso[riffusion]`       |
| **Stable Audio 3**         | Local (MLX runtime, Apple Silicon)                | None                                 | runtime: see below                    |
| **Magenta RealTime 2**     | Local (MLX runtime, Apple Silicon)                | None                                 | runtime: see below                    |
| **Foundation-1**           | Local (stable-audio-tools, own environment)       | None                                 | built on first use: see below         |

| **Suno** (via sunoapi.org) | REST API                                          | `SUNO_API_KEY`                       | `pip install arioso[sunoapi]`         |

```python
# See what's available
arioso.list_platforms()
# ['beatoven', 'elevenlabs', 'harmonai', 'jen', 'loudly', 'lyria2', ...]

# Inspect a platform's configuration
arioso.get_platform_info("musicgen")
```

### MusicGen (local, no API key)

Runs on your machine, with one of three libraries:

- **MLX** (Apple Silicon, text prompts): Apple’s port in `ml-explore/mlx-examples`, run in its own environment by a worker. On an M1 Max a 10 s clip of `musicgen-small` takes about 11 s, against 3 to 6 minutes with `transformers` on the GPU. It is used for text takes whenever its runtime is installed:
  ```default
  git init --quiet ~/.local/share/arioso/runtimes/mlx-examples
  git -C ~/.local/share/arioso/runtimes/mlx-examples fetch --quiet --depth 1 https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-examples 796f5b53cab69a3d48a44233ce21aae889e94a08
  git -C ~/.local/share/arioso/runtimes/mlx-examples checkout --quiet --detach 796f5b53cab69a3d48a44233ce21aae889e94a08
  cd ~/.local/share/arioso/runtimes/mlx-examples/musicgen && uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt
  ```

  (or point `$ARIOSO_MLX_EXAMPLES_DIR` at an existing checkout). The checkout is pinned to that commit, the one arioso was measured on: a runtime at another commit is not used for automatic selection (arioso warns and falls back to the next backend), and the error says how to move it. `python -c "from arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends import MlxBackend; print(MlxBackend.runtime().hint())"` prints the commands for the current pin. It runs Meta’s mono text checkpoints (`facebook/musicgen-small`, `-medium`, `-large`); `top_p` is ignored there, and takes past MusicGen’s 30 s context are warned about. Alternating text takes with melody or continuation takes reloads a model at each switch, so batch them by kind.
- **audiocraft**, Meta’s library, when it imports.
- **transformers** otherwise. On Apple Silicon the text checkpoints run on the CPU unless `ARIOSO_TORCH_DEVICE=mps`: on MPS they were slower than the CPU and grew GPU memory with every step. The melody checkpoint keeps MPS.

Melody-following and continuation always use audiocraft or transformers. `ARIOSO_MUSICGEN_BACKEND=mlx|audiocraft|transformers` forces one (`mlx` for text takes only).

```python
song = arioso.generate(
    "chill lofi beats",
    platform="musicgen",
    duration=10,
    temperature=0.8,
    guidance=3.0,
    model="facebook/musicgen-small",  # or medium, large, melody
)
```

### Local models in their own environments (Stable Audio 3, Magenta RealTime 2, ACE-Step 1.5)

Some local models pin library versions (MLX, torch) that cannot share an environment with each other, so arioso runs them in their own: each platform names a runtime directory and the commands that install it, and a missing one raises `RuntimeNotInstalled` with those commands. Runtimes live under `~/.local/share/arioso/runtimes/<name>` unless `$ARIOSO_RUNTIMES_DIR` or the platform’s own variable (`$ARIOSO_SA3_DIR`, `$ARIOSO_MAGENTA_RT_DIR`, `$ARIOSO_ACE_STEP_DIR`, `$ARIOSO_MLX_EXAMPLES_DIR` for MusicGen on MLX) points elsewhere. Magenta RealTime, ACE-Step and MusicGen on MLX keep one worker process alive, so the model loads once per session.

```python
import arioso

# Stable Audio 3 (Stability's MLX build, Apple Silicon): model="sm-music" (default), "sm-sfx" or "medium"
song = arioso.generate(
    "lo-fi hip hop loop, 85 BPM, mellow Rhodes",
    platform="stable_audio_3",
    duration=11.29,
    seed=1,
)

# Magenta RealTime 2 (MLX, Apple Silicon): style from text or from a reference clip
song = arioso.generate("funky drum and bass groove", platform="magenta_rt", duration=10)

# ACE-Step 1.5 run locally (fal.ai stays the default; $ARIOSO_ACE_STEP_RUNTIME=local changes it): explicit BPM and key
song = arioso.generate(
    "acoustic guitar and soft piano",
    platform="ace_step",
    runtime="local",
    bpm=100,
    key="C Major",
    duration=30,
)
```

| platform           | weights licence                                                     | commercial use                  |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| `stable_audio_3`   | Stability AI Community License (+ Gemma terms for its text encoder) | free under US$1M annual revenue |
| `magenta_rt`       | CC-BY-4.0                                                           | yes, with attribution           |
| `ace_step` (local) | MIT                                                                 | yes                             |
| `foundation_1`     | Stability AI Community License                                      | free under US$1M annual revenue |

### Foundation-1 (local loops and one-shots, stable-audio-tools)

[Foundation-1](https://huggingface.co/RoyalCities/Foundation-1) is a Stable Audio Open 1.0 fine-tune for instrument loops and one-shots, prompted with tags: instrument family and sub-family, timbre, notation and FX, then bars, tempo and key (`"Synth Lead, Warm, Arp, Medium Reverb, 8 Bars, 140 BPM, E minor"`; the tag list is in the model card’s `Master_Tag_Reference.md`). The prompt is passed through; `bpm` and `key` are appended as those tags. With a tempo the clip is exactly `bars` bars of 4/4 (`bars=4` or `8`, else the count nearest to `duration`); without one, `duration` is the clip length (at most 20 s). Tags already in the prompt are read (a short key such as `Am` is spelt out; a contradiction with the arguments is an error), and missing ones go in the card’s order. `note="C3"` makes a one-shot at that pitch (`Target Note, C3` appended, 3 s by default). Three checkpoints share one model: `model="foundation-1"` (loops, the default), `"1.2-samples"` (loops and one-shots) and `"1.2-keybeds"` (pitch-consistent one-shots; with `note=` the prompt takes that checkpoint’s single-note form, `Keybed, Timbre Profile, ..., Target Note, C3`).

stable-audio-tools pins its own torch and Python 3.10, so arioso builds an environment for it with `uv` on first use (once, under `~/.local/share/arioso/envs/foundation-1`, or `$ARIOSO_ENVS_DIR`; `$ARIOSO_FOUNDATION_1_ENV` names an existing one instead) from pinned requirements resolved with `--exclude-newer`, and runs the model in one worker process there. Each checkpoint (2.4 GB) and the T5-base text encoder download once to the Hugging Face cache, at pinned revisions, and are read from it without network calls afterwards. On a Mac it needs Apple Silicon (torch 2.7 has no Intel macOS wheels). It runs on CUDA, Apple MPS or the CPU (`device=` to choose). On MPS it samples with plain classifier-free guidance, as Stable Audio Open does: stable-audio-tools’ default adaptive projected guidance computes in float64, which MPS does not support, so it is turned off, and `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1` lets any operator MPS lacks run on the CPU.

```python
import arioso

# A 4-bar loop at 100 BPM in A minor (9.6 s)
song = arioso.generate(
    "Rhodes Piano, Warm, Chord Progression, Low Reverb",
    platform="foundation_1",
    bpm=100,
    key="Am",
    bars=4,
    seed=7,
)
song.metadata[
    "prompt_sent"
]  # 'Rhodes Piano, Warm, Chord Progression, Low Reverb, 4 Bars, 100 BPM, A minor'

# A one-shot: no tempo, so duration is the length
song = arioso.generate(
    "Grand Piano, Near, Bright, Hit",
    platform="foundation_1",
    model="1.2-samples",
    duration=3,
)
```

Measured on an M1 Max (64 GB, MPS, the default 100 steps): a 10 s clip takes 70 s once the model is loaded (92 s for the first, loading included), about 7 times real time, and the worker process peaks at 14 GB.

Building playable sampler instruments from the keybeds checkpoint (many notes from one descriptor, sliced and mapped) is not covered yet: see [#66](https://github.com/thorwhalen/arioso/issues/66).

### ElevenLabs

Needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` environment variable.

```python
song = arioso.generate(
    "dramatic film score",
    platform="elevenlabs",
    duration=60,
    instrumental=True,
    output_format="mp3_44100_128",
)

# With lyrics
song = arioso.generate(
    "pop ballad",
    platform="elevenlabs",
    lyrics="[Verse]\nWalking through the rain\n[Chorus]\nI found my way home",
    title="Coming Home",
)
```

### Suno (via sunoapi.org)

Needs `SUNO_API_KEY` environment variable.

```python
songs = arioso.generate_many(
    "summer reggae vibes",
    platform="sunoapi",
    genre="reggae, tropical",
    instrumental=True,
)
# Suno returns 2 songs per call
for song in songs:
    print(song.title, song.audio_url)
```

## Parameters

All platforms share a common vocabulary of parameter names. Use any that
the platform supports — unsupported ones are warned about and ignored.

```python
song = arioso.generate(
    "ambient soundscape",  # prompt (required)
    platform="musicgen",
    duration=15,  # seconds
    temperature=1.2,  # sampling randomness
    top_k=250,  # top-k sampling
    guidance=3.0,  # classifier-free guidance
    seed=42,  # reproducibility
)
```

The full set of unified parameter names (42):

| Parameter       | Type   | Description                         |
|-----------------|--------|-------------------------------------|
| `prompt`        | str    | Text description of desired music   |
| `duration`      | float  | Output length in seconds            |
| `lyrics`        | str    | Custom lyrics text                  |
| `instrumental`  | bool   | Force instrumental-only output      |
| `genre`         | str    | Genre tag or category               |
| `title`         | str    | Song title                          |
| `model`         | str    | Model version or variant            |
| `seed`          | int    | Random seed for reproducibility     |
| `guidance`      | float  | Classifier-free guidance scale      |
| `temperature`   | float  | Sampling randomness                 |
| `top_k`         | int    | Top-k sampling parameter            |
| `top_p`         | float  | Top-p (nucleus) sampling            |
| `bpm`           | int    | Beats per minute                    |
| `key`           | str    | Musical key (e.g. “C major”)        |
| `energy`        | float  | Energy/intensity level 0-1          |
| `output_format` | str    | Desired output format               |
| …               |        | See `arioso.AFFORDANCES` for all 40 |

Each platform maps these to its native parameter names automatically.
For example, `instrumental=True` becomes `make_instrumental=True` for Suno
and `force_instrumental=True` for ElevenLabs.

### Parameter schemas (for forms, agents and validators)

`arioso.param_schema(platform)` returns the parameters a platform accepts as JSON Schema: each one’s type, bounds or choices, a title and a description. Unified names are marked `"x-arioso": {"group": "common"}`; parameters only that platform has (Suno’s `weirdness`, `style_weight`, `vocal_gender`, …) are marked `"extra"`. A front end can render the common part once and reveal a platform’s extras when it is selected.

```python
schema = arioso.param_schema("sunoapi")
schema["properties"][
    "audio_input_strength"
]  # {'type': 'number', 'minimum': 0, 'maximum': 1, 'title': 'Audio Influence', ...}
schema["x-arioso"]["extra"]  # ['weirdness', 'style_weight', 'vocal_gender', 'variety']
arioso.common_params(["sunoapi", "elevenlabs"])  # the names both accept
```

From a shell: `arioso schema sunoapi`.

## Output

Every call returns a `Song` object:

```python
song = arioso.generate("jazz piano", platform="musicgen")

song.status  # 'complete'
song.platform  # 'musicgen'
song.title  # ''
song.metadata  # {'model': 'facebook/musicgen-small', ...}

# Audio is in song.audio (an AudioResult)
song.audio.audio_array  # numpy array (local models)
song.audio.audio_bytes  # raw bytes (REST APIs)
song.audio.audio_url  # URL string (Suno)
song.audio.sample_rate  # e.g. 32000
song.audio.format  # 'wav', 'mp3', etc.

# Shortcuts
song.audio_array  # same as song.audio.audio_array
song.audio_bytes  # same as song.audio.audio_bytes
song.sample_rate  # same as song.audio.sample_rate
```

Use `generate_many()` when you want all results (some platforms return multiple):

```python
songs = arioso.generate_many("pop song", platform="sunoapi")
# Returns list[Song]
```

## Adding a new platform

Arioso uses a plugin architecture. Each platform is a subfolder under
`arioso/platforms/` with two files:

```default
arioso/platforms/myplatform/
    __init__.py
    config.py        # required: declares PLATFORM_CONFIG
    adapter.py       # optional: custom generation logic
```

### Minimal example (REST API)

For a REST API, you may only need `config.py`:

```python
# arioso/platforms/myplatform/config.py

PLATFORM_CONFIG = {
    "name": "myplatform",
    "display_name": "My Platform",
    "website": "https://myplatform.com",
    "tier": "simple",
    "access_type": "rest_api",
    "auth": {
        "type": "bearer_token",
        "env_var": "MYPLATFORM_API_KEY",
    },
    "param_map": {
        "prompt": {"native_name": "text", "required": True},
        "duration": {"native_name": "length_seconds"},
    },
    "supported_affordances": ["prompt", "duration"],
    "on_unsupported_param": "warn",
    "output": {
        "default_format": "mp3",
        "sample_rate": 44100,
        "returns": "bytes",
    },
    "api": {
        "base_url": "https://api.myplatform.com",
        "generate_endpoint": {"method": "post", "path": "/v1/generate"},
    },
}
```

The platform is auto-discovered on the next `arioso.list_platforms()` call.

### Custom adapter (Python library)

For platforms that are Python libraries rather than REST APIs, add an `adapter.py`:

```python
# arioso/platforms/myplatform/adapter.py

from arioso.base import Song, AudioResult


class Adapter:
    def __init__(self, config):
        self.config = config

    def generate(self, prompt, *, duration=10, **kwargs):
        # Your generation logic here
        from some_library import generate_audio

        audio = generate_audio(prompt, length=duration)

        return Song(
            audio=AudioResult(audio_array=audio, sample_rate=44100, format="wav"),
            platform="myplatform",
            status="complete",
        )
```

### Manual registration

Third-party packages can register platforms at runtime:

```python
from arioso.registry import register_platform

register_platform("custom", my_config_dict, my_adapter_instance)
```

## Platforms Without Public APIs

The following platforms were considered during the design of arioso’s unified
parameter vocabulary and affordance system, but do not have public APIs (nor a
reliable third-party API wrapper). They are listed here for completeness.

| Platform       | Website                                  | What It Does                                                                                           | Affordances Considered                 |
|----------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| **AIVA**       | [aiva.ai](https://aiva.ai)               | Orchestral AI composition. Desktop/web DAW with 250+ style presets, direct BPM/key/instrument control. | genre, bpm, key, instruments, duration |
| **ACE Studio** | [acestudio.ai](https://acestudio.ai)     | AI vocal synthesis DAW plugin. 140+ voice models for singing voice generation.                         | voice_id, lyrics, instruments          |
| **Boomy**      | [boomy.com](https://boomy.com)           | AI song creation with Auto Vocal and streaming platform distribution. Enterprise-only API.             | prompt, voice_id, instrumental         |
| **Soundraw**   | [soundraw.io](https://soundraw.io)       | AI music generation for content creators. Enterprise B2B API only ($11/mo consumer web app).           | genre, duration, energy                |
| **CassetteAI** | [cassetteai.com](https://cassetteai.com) | Prompt-based music generation. Web-only, no known API.                                                 | prompt, duration                       |
| **Musicfy**    | [musicfy.lol](https://musicfy.lol)       | AI music generation with voice cloning and pitch shifting. Web-only, no known API.                     | prompt, voice_id, pitch_shift          |

## Research & Background

Arioso’s design is informed by extensive research into the AI music generation
landscape. Two reference documents in [`misc/docs/`]() provide the
full background:

### Platform comparison and API landscape

[**AI Music Generation Tools: A Unified API Reference for 21 Platforms**]()
maps the full union of capabilities across every tool we investigated. Highlights:

- [General characteristics comparison]() —
  pricing, API availability, max length, sample rate, vocal support, and quality tier for 18 tools
- [Documentation and integration links]() —
  docs URLs, OpenAPI specs, Python/JS SDKs, and MCP servers per platform
- [Feature affordance matrix]() —
  which platforms support text prompts, negative prompts, lyrics, audio conditioning, melody conditioning, duration, BPM, key, genre tags, energy, instruments, and more
- [Unified affordance mapping]() —
  the 40 common parameter names that arioso exposes, with native parameter names per platform
- [Complete API parameter catalogs]() —
  full endpoint and parameter documentation for Suno, ElevenLabs, MusicGen, Lyria RealTime, Stable Audio Open, and YuE

### Prompt engineering across platforms

[**Prompt Engineering for Music AI Generation: A Resource Guide**]()
compiles 78 resources (papers, datasets, tools, taxonomies, and guides) covering
how to write effective prompts for text-to-music systems. Key sections:

- [Papers on prompt engineering techniques]() —
  chain-of-thought prompting, prompt tuning, user studies, and structured prompting strategies
- [Model architecture and text encoders]() —
  how T5, CLAP, FLAN-T5, and MuLan encoders determine which prompt styles work best
- [Text-audio alignment models]() —
  CLAP, MuLan, LAION-CLAP, and how they shape the vocabulary space
- [CFG and parameter interactions]() —
  how guidance scale, temperature, and other parameters interact with text prompts
- [Captioning datasets defining vocabulary]() —
  MusicCaps, LP-MusicCaps, MusicBench, and 11 other datasets that trained these models
- [Vocabulary and taxonomy resources]() —
  AudioSet ontology, Music Ontology, Cyanite AI taxonomy
- [Platform-specific prompt guides]() —
  official and community guides for Stable Audio, Udio, Lyria, Suno, ElevenLabs, and more

Each platform also has a `<PLATFORM>_REFERENCE.md` in its directory under
`arioso/platforms/` with platform-specific prompt engineering guidance, API
details, and links to further reading.

## Architecture

```default
arioso/
    __init__.py          # Facade: generate(), list_platforms()
    base.py              # Song, AudioResult, AFFORDANCES (42 unified params)
    registry.py          # Auto-discovery, lazy loading, manual registration
    translation.py       # Parameter renaming & coercion (common -> native)
    _util.py             # Auth helpers, HTTP session factory

    platforms/
        _base_adapter.py   # BaseRestAdapter (shared REST infrastructure)
        musicgen/          # Local inference via audiocraft/transformers
        stable_audio/      # Local inference via diffusers
        harmonai/          # Unconditional generation via Dance Diffusion
        riffusion/         # Spectrogram-based via diffusers
        elevenlabs/        # REST with OpenAPI spec via ho
        sunoapi/           # REST via sunoapi.org
        lyria2/            # Google Vertex AI REST
        lyria_rt/          # Google Lyria RealTime WebSocket
        mubert/            # Mubert REST API
        beatoven/          # Beatoven.ai REST API
        loudly/            # Loudly REST API
        jen/               # Jen REST API
        yue/               # YuE via fal.ai or local CLI
        stable_audio_25/   # Stable Audio 2.5 via fal.ai (audio-to-audio with strength)
        ace_step/          # ACE-Step via fal.ai (tags -> music, audio remix)
        udio/              # Udio via unofficial wrapper
```

Key design choices:

- **Zero required dependencies.** The core package imports nothing outside stdlib.
  Platform dependencies are lazy-imported when you first call `generate()`.
- **Config-driven plugins.** Each platform declares a `PLATFORM_CONFIG` dict with
  parameter mappings, auth scheme, endpoints, and output format. Adding a platform
  is mostly configuration.
- **Automatic parameter translation.** The translation layer renames unified
  affordance names to native platform names and applies type coercions
  (e.g. `duration` seconds to `music_length_ms` milliseconds for ElevenLabs)
  for platforms served by the config-generated REST adapter. A platform with its
  own `adapter.py` takes unified names directly, on every path
  (`arioso.generate` and `arioso.services.<platform>.generate` alike).
- **Leverages existing libraries.** Uses
  [ho](https://github.com/i2mint/ho) for OpenAPI-to-Python-function generation,
  [i2](https://github.com/i2mint/i2) for signature manipulation and function wrapping.

(`"no"`), allows it under conditions such as a revenue cap or use

# arioso.cli

The functions behind the `arioso` command line.

### Functions

| [`compare`](_autosummary/arioso.cli.html.md#arioso.cli.compare)(contenders, \*[, prompts, duration, ...])   | Render the same prompts with several platforms; time, measure and check each take.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`generate`](_autosummary/arioso.cli.html.md#arioso.cli.generate)(prompt, \*[, platform, duration, ...])     | Generate music from a text prompt and write it to a file.                            |

### arioso.cli.commands *= {'compare': <function compare>, 'generate': <function generate>, 'platforms': <function platforms>, 'schema': <function schema>}*

The commands of the `arioso` command line (the SSOT its parser is built from).

### arioso.cli.compare(contenders, , prompts=None, duration=10.0, seed=0, out_dir='arioso_compare', warmup=2.0, allow_hosted=False, min_free_gb=None, timeout=None, preload=None, no_page=False)

Render the same prompts with several platforms; time, measure and check each take.

Each contender runs in its own process, one after the other, with one progress line per
take on stderr. Takes go to `<out_dir>/<run>/<contender>/`, one JSON line per take to
`<out_dir>/results.jsonl`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **contenders** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Comma-separated platforms, each optionally with options:
    `stable_audio_3,magenta_rt,ace_step:runtime=local`.
  * **prompts** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A JSON file holding a list of prompts (`text`, and optionally `id`,
    `bpm`, `key`, `melody`, `duration`); default: three built-in prompts.
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds asked of each take.
  * **seed** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Random seed, on platforms that take one.
  * **out_dir** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Where takes, records and the page go.
  * **warmup** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds generated once per contender before the timed takes (0: none).
  * **allow_hosted** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Allow platforms that call a paid hosted service.
  * **min_free_gb** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Skip a contender when less memory than this is available.
  * **timeout** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds a contender may run before it is killed (with its workers).
  * **preload** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Comma-separated modules (`module` or `module:function`) that
    register third-party platforms.
  * **no_page** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Do not write `<out_dir>/<run>/index.html` (a page of players).
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]
* **Returns:**
  A summary table, one line per contender, then the paths written.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – When every take failed (the command exits 1).

### arioso.cli.generate(prompt, , platform='musicgen', duration=None, output='out.wav', model=None, seed=None)

Generate music from a text prompt and write it to a file.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description of the music.
  * **platform** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The platform to generate with (see `arioso platforms`).

    encoded audio from a hosted platform keeps its own format; either
    way the suffix follows the format.
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The platform’s model or checkpoint, when it offers a choice.
  * **seed** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Random seed, on platforms that take one.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Returns:**
  The path written.

# _autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md

# arioso.compare

Compare platforms on the same prompts: time, memory and objective checks, as records.

Choosing a local model is a measurement. [`compare()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.compare) renders every prompt with every
contender and yields one flat record per take: wall time (model load plus warm-up, then per
take), real-time factor, peak memory, and objective checks of the audio (detected tempo
against the BPM asked for, estimated key against the key asked for, clipping, level):

```default
import arioso.compare as ac

records = list(ac.compare(["stable_audio_3", "magenta_rt", "ace_step:runtime=local"]))
ac.compare_page(records, "arioso_compare/index.html")
```

or, from the shell:

```default
arioso compare stable_audio_3,magenta_rt,ace_step:runtime=local --prompts prompts.json
```

The records are the single source of truth: they are appended to `<out_dir>/results.jsonl`
as they come, the command prints a summary of them, and [`compare_page()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.compare_page) renders them as a
page of players. Each contender runs in a fresh child process (see [`in_child_process()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.in_child_process)),
one after the other, so only one model is in memory at a time and each one’s peak memory is
its own.

A **contender** is a platform plus the options it is called with, written
`platform[:key=value[:key=value...]]` (values are read as JSON when they parse, so
`num_steps=8` is an int): `ace_step:runtime=local`, `musicgen:model=facebook/musicgen-small`.

A **prompt** is a dict: `text` (required), `id`, and optionally `bpm`, `key` (`"C
major"`), `melody` (an audio file, passed to platforms that take a melody) and
`duration`. [`DFLT_PROMPTS`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.DFLT_PROMPTS) is a small set covering a groove, an accompaniment and a
loop.

Hosted platforms cost money per call, so [`compare()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.compare) refuses them unless
`allow_hosted=True` ([`is_hosted()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.is_hosted) says which those are).

Seams, all keyword arguments: `runner` (how one contender is run and measured:
[`in_child_process()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.in_child_process) or [`in_this_process()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.in_this_process)), `scorer` (audio to a dict of checks:
[`objective_checks()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.objective_checks)), and `min_free_gb` (refuse to start a contender when the machine
has less memory available than that).

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_PROMPTS`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.DFLT_PROMPTS)       | a groove at a tempo, an accompaniment in a key, a loop.                                 |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_WARMUP`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.DFLT_WARMUP)        | Seconds of audio generated once before the timed takes, so load is not counted in them. |
| [`LOCAL_ACCESS_TYPES`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.LOCAL_ACCESS_TYPES) | The `access_type` values of platforms that run on this machine.                         |

### Functions

| [`compare`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.compare)(contenders[, prompts, duration, ...])   | Render every prompt with every contender; yield one record per take.                                                  |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`compare_page`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.compare_page)(records[, path, title, prompts])   | Write a self-contained HTML page: a summary table, then each prompt's takes as players.                               |
| [`in_child_process`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.in_child_process)(contender, prompts, \*, ...)   | Run `contender` in a fresh `python -m arioso.compare` process (the default runner).                                   |
| [`in_this_process`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.in_this_process)(contender, prompts, \*, ...)    | Run `contender` on `prompts` here; one record per prompt, audio under `out_dir`.                                      |
| [`is_hosted`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.is_hosted)(contender)                            | Whether a contender may call a hosted (paid, per call) service rather than a local model.                             |
| [`key_agreement`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.key_agreement)(detected, asked)                  | `"exact"`, `"relative"` (C major vs A minor), `"other"`, or `None` if unparsable.                                     |
| [`load_prompts`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.load_prompts)([source])                          | Prompts from a JSON file (a list of dicts), a list, or [`DFLT_PROMPTS`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.DFLT_PROMPTS). |
| [`objective_checks`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.objective_checks)(y, sr, prompt)                 | Checks a listener would otherwise make by ear: level, clipping, tempo, key.                                           |
| [`parse_contenders`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.parse_contenders)(specs)                         | Contenders from a comma-separated string or an iterable of specs.                                                     |

### Classes

| [`Contender`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.Contender)(platform[, options, label])   | A platform and the options it is called with; `label` names it in records.   |

### *class* arioso.compare.Contender(platform, options=dict(), label='')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A platform and the options it is called with; `label` names it in records.

#### *classmethod* parse(spec)

`"ace_step:runtime=local:num_steps=8"` -> `Contender("ace_step", {...})`.

```pycon
>>> Contender.parse("ace_step:runtime=local:num_steps=8").options
{'runtime': 'local', 'num_steps': 8}
```

  [`Contender`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.Contender)

### arioso.compare.DFLT_PROMPTS *= ({'bpm': 100, 'id': 'groove100', 'text': 'funky drum and bass groove at 100 BPM, tight hi-hats, punchy kick, warm electric bass, steady pocket, instrumental'}, {'bpm': 100, 'id': 'accomp', 'key': 'C major', 'text': 'gentle acoustic guitar and soft piano accompaniment, 100 BPM, C major, warm and simple, instrumental'}, {'bpm': 85, 'id': 'loop85', 'text': '4-bar lo-fi hip hop loop, 85 BPM, mellow Rhodes chords, dusty drums, vinyl crackle, seamless loop, instrumental'})*

a groove at a tempo, an accompaniment in a key, a loop.

### arioso.compare.LOCAL_ACCESS_TYPES *= frozenset({'local_runtime', 'python_lib'})*

The `access_type` values of platforms that run on this machine.

### arioso.compare.compare(contenders, prompts=None, \*, duration=10.0, seed=0, out_dir='arioso_compare', warmup=2.0, runner=None, scorer=<function objective_checks>, allow_hosted=False, min_free_gb=None, preload=(), timeout=None, run_id=None)

Render every prompt with every contender; yield one record per take.

* **Parameters:**
  * **contenders** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Contender`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.Contender)]) – Platform specs (`"ace_step:runtime=local"`, see [`Contender`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.Contender)),
    comma-separated or as an iterable.
  * **prompts** – A JSON file, a list of prompt dicts, or `None` for [`DFLT_PROMPTS`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.DFLT_PROMPTS).
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds asked of each take (a prompt’s own `duration` wins).
  * **seed** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Passed to platforms that take one (`None`: don’t).
  * **out_dir** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – Takes go to `<out_dir>/<run_id>/<contender>/<prompt id>.wav`; records
    are appended to `<out_dir>/results.jsonl` (one file for every run).
  * **warmup** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Seconds generated once per contender before the timed takes (`0`/`None`:
    no warm-up, so the first take’s time includes loading the model).
  * **runner** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]]]) – Runs one contender: [`in_child_process()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.in_child_process) (`None`, the default) or
    [`in_this_process()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.in_this_process), or any callable with their signature.
  * **scorer** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]]) – `(audio, sample_rate, prompt) -> dict` merged into each record; `None`
    for no checks.
  * **allow_hosted** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Allow contenders that call paid hosted services ([`is_hosted()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.is_hosted)).
  * **min_free_gb** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – When the machine has less memory available than this before a
    contender starts, record that contender as an error instead of running it.
  * **preload** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Modules (`"module"` or `"module:function"`) that make third-party
    platforms known, run here before anything is checked and passed to a runner
    that takes `preload` (the child process runs them too).
  * **timeout** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Seconds a contender may run before it is killed with every process it
    started, passed to a runner that takes `timeout` (the default one does).
  * **run_id** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Names this run in its records and its folder (default: the start time).
* **Yields:**
  *Flat dicts* – `contender`, `platform`, `options`, `prompt`, timings
  (`load_s`, `gen_s`, `rtf`), memory (`peak_memory_gb`,
  `workers_peak_memory_gb`, `available_memory_gb`), `path`, the scorer’s
  checks, `error` when a take failed, and the machine.
* **Return type:**
  [*Iterator*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### arioso.compare.compare_page(records, path=PosixPath('arioso_compare/index.html'), , title='Music generation compared', prompts=None)

Write a self-contained HTML page: a summary table, then each prompt’s takes as players.

Audio is linked relative to the page, so keep the page beside the takes (the default
`<out_dir>/index.html`) and publish the folder.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### arioso.compare.in_child_process(contender, prompts, , duration, seed, out_dir, warmup, python=None, preload=(), timeout=None)

Run `contender` in a fresh `python -m arioso.compare` process (the default runner).

A fresh process per contender frees the previous model’s memory before the next loads,
and makes the process’s lifetime peak memory that contender’s own. `python` is the
interpreter (default: this one); `preload` names what the child runs first, to make
third-party platforms known: `"module"` is imported, `"module:function"` is imported
and `function()` called. The child’s output goes to `<out_dir>/<contender>/child.log`.
The child writes each take’s record as soon as it is made, so a child killed after
`timeout` seconds (with every process it started) or exiting non-zero still returns
the takes it finished, each marked with `child_exit`; prompts it never reached get an
`error`. Processes the child started are killed when it ends, however it ends; on
Windows only when it is killed (thorwhalen/ps#25).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### arioso.compare.in_this_process(contender, prompts, , duration, seed, out_dir, warmup, on_record=None)

Run `contender` on `prompts` here; one record per prompt, audio under `out_dir`.

A take that fails becomes a record with an `error` (the others still run); a contender
that fails its warm-up makes every record an error. `peak_memory_gb` is this process’s
lifetime peak, so run each contender in a fresh process ([`in_child_process()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.in_child_process)) to
attribute it; `workers_peak_memory_gb` is the peak of the processes it started (a local
runtime’s worker, or one process per take), sampled while it ran (see
`PeakSampler`; here its exit-time floor also covers children of
earlier contenders run in this process). `on_record` is called with each take’s record
as soon as it is made, before the memory figures are added at the end.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### arioso.compare.is_hosted(contender)

Whether a contender may call a hosted (paid, per call) service rather than a local model.

Errs on the side of caution. Local means: `access_type` is `python_lib` or
`local_runtime` (a missing one is the translation layer’s `rest_api`), the terms are
not the provider’s, no credential is taken (even an optional one: `yue` calls fal.ai
whenever `FAL_KEY` is set), and no fal model is declared. Anything else is hosted,
unless the contender asks for `runtime="local"` *and* the platform declares a local
runtime (`ace_step`); on any other platform that option is ignored, so it changes
nothing here either.

```pycon
>>> is_hosted("elevenlabs"), is_hosted("stable_audio_3"), is_hosted("ace_step:runtime=local")
(True, False, False)
>>> is_hosted("elevenlabs:runtime=local")
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### arioso.compare.key_agreement(detected, asked)

`"exact"`, `"relative"` (C major vs A minor), `"other"`, or `None` if unparsable.

```pycon
>>> key_agreement("A minor", "C major"), key_agreement("c major", "C Major")
('relative', 'exact')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### arioso.compare.load_prompts(source=None)

Prompts from a JSON file (a list of dicts), a list, or [`DFLT_PROMPTS`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.DFLT_PROMPTS).

A `melody` path in a file is read relative to that file. Prompts without an `id`
get `p0`, `p1`…

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### arioso.compare.objective_checks(y, sr, prompt)

Checks a listener would otherwise make by ear: level, clipping, tempo, key.

Level and clipping need numpy only. Tempo comes from `denote.get_beats` and key from
`denote.get_key` when `denote` provides them; a check that cannot run goes into
`checks_skipped` (check name to reason) instead of failing the take.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### arioso.compare.parse_contenders(specs)

Contenders from a comma-separated string or an iterable of specs.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Contender`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.Contender)]

### arioso.compare.read_records(out_dir='arioso_compare')

The records in `<out_dir>/results.jsonl`, keeping the latest per (contender, prompt).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### arioso.compare.summarize(records)

One row per contender: takes, failures, median RTF, load, peak memory, check rates.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### arioso.compare.summary_lines(records)

[`summarize()`](_autosummary/arioso.compare.html.md#arioso.compare.summarize) as aligned text lines, a header first.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### arioso.compare.tempo_error(detected, asked)

Relative tempo error, forgiving the half/double-time slips beat trackers make.

```pycon

(0.0, 0.1)
```

# _autosummary/arioso.html.md

# arioso

Arioso - Unified facade for AI music generation platforms.

Usage:

```default
import arioso

# Generate with the default platform (musicgen)
song = arioso.generate("upbeat jazz piano", duration=10)

# Generate with a specific platform
song = arioso.generate("epic orchestral", platform="elevenlabs", duration=30)

# List available platforms
arioso.list_platforms()  # ['musicgen', 'sunoapi', 'elevenlabs', ...]

# Get platform config
arioso.get_platform_info("musicgen")

# Every platform with its access type and weights licence
arioso.platform_table()

# The parameters a platform accepts, as JSON Schema (common + its extras)
arioso.param_schema("sunoapi")

# Rich platform access via services
s = arioso.services.sunoapi
s.generate("jazz piano", duration=30)       # unified names
s.native_generate("jazz", genre="jazz")     # native names
s.upload_file("/path/to/audio.mp3")         # platform-specific

# Cross-platform slices
arioso.generators["sunoapi"]("jazz")
arioso.generators.sunoapi("jazz")
```

### Module Attributes

| [`AUDIO_INPUT_AFFORDANCES`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.AUDIO_INPUT_AFFORDANCES)   | Affordances that carry caller-supplied *input* audio (used by [`enhance()`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.enhance)).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`PLATFORM_TABLE_FIELDS`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.PLATFORM_TABLE_FIELDS)     | The config fields [`platform_table()`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.platform_table) reports, in column order.                |

### Functions

| [`check_status`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.check_status)(song)                                | Check the current status of a pending Song and return updated Songs.       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`enhance`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.enhance)(audio[, prompt, platform, strength, as_]) | Transform existing audio into AI-enhanced audio (pipeline stage 3->4).     |
| [`fetch_audio`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.fetch_audio)(song)                                 | Download the audio bytes for a Song that has an audio_url.                 |
| [`generate`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.generate)(prompt, \*[, platform])                  | Generate music using the specified platform.                               |
| [`generate_many`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.generate_many)(prompt, \*[, platform])             | Generate music, returning all results (some platforms return multiple).    |
| [`get_platform_info`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.get_platform_info)(name)                           | Get configuration info for a platform.                                     |
| [`list_platforms`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.list_platforms)()                                  | Return names of all available platforms.                                   |
| [`platform_table`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.platform_table)(\*[, fields])                      | One row per platform: its access type, weights licence and commercial use. |
| [`supports_audio_input`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.supports_audio_input)(platform)                    | Whether *platform* can condition on caller-supplied input audio.           |

### arioso.AUDIO_INPUT_AFFORDANCES *= ('audio_input', 'melody', 'reference_audio')*

Affordances that carry caller-supplied *input* audio (used by [`enhance()`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.enhance)).
Distinct from the clip-extension affordance `continue_from`, which extends
a track rather than conditioning on one (a prior generation’s id/URL on
hosted platforms, the audio itself on musicgen).

### arioso.PLATFORM_TABLE_FIELDS *= ('name', 'access_type', 'weights_license', 'commercial_use')*

The config fields [`platform_table()`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.platform_table) reports, in column order.

### arioso.check_status(song)

Check the current status of a pending Song and return updated Songs.

For platforms that use async/callback-based generation (like sunoapi),
this polls the platform’s status endpoint to get the latest state,
including audio URLs once generation is complete.

* **Parameters:**
  **song** ([`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)) – A Song object (typically with status=’pending’).
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)]
* **Returns:**
  List of updated Song objects with current status and audio URLs.

Example:

```default
songs = arioso.generate_many("reggae", platform="sunoapi", ...)
# ... wait a bit ...
updated = arioso.check_status(songs[0])
if updated[0].status == "complete":
    print(updated[0].audio_url)
```

### arioso.enhance(audio, prompt='', , platform='stable_audio', strength=None, as_='auto', \*\*kwargs)

Transform existing audio into AI-enhanced audio (pipeline stage 3->4).

Progressive-disclosure sugar over [`generate()`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.generate): routes *audio* into the
platform’s audio-conditioning affordance and generates. This is the entry
point for the “rendered MIDI audio -> AI-enhanced audio” step.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – The input audio to transform – a [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song),
    [`AudioResult`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.AudioResult), `bytes`, a file path, an
    `(array, sample_rate)` pair, or a NumPy waveform (normalized by
    `arioso._audio.to_audio_ref`).
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Optional text guiding the transformation.
  * **platform** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – An audio-capable platform (default `'stable_audio'`); verify
    with [`supports_audio_input()`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.supports_audio_input).
  * **strength** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – How much the input audio influences the output (0-1), where the
    platform supports it. (Note: `stable_audio` via diffusers has no
    strength knob and will warn if one is passed.)
  * **as_** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Which affordance to route *audio* into – `'auto'` (default; picks
    `audio_input` > `melody` > `reference_audio`) or an explicit
    affordance name from [`AUDIO_INPUT_AFFORDANCES`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.AUDIO_INPUT_AFFORDANCES).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Further unified affordance parameters (duration, seed, …).
* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)
* **Returns:**
  A [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song) with the enhanced audio.

Example:

```default
rendered = ...  # a Song from a score2audio render
better = arioso.enhance(rendered, "warm analog studio band")
```

### arioso.fetch_audio(song)

Download the audio bytes for a Song that has an audio_url.

* **Parameters:**
  **song** ([`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)) – A Song with a populated audio_url (status=’complete’).
* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)
* **Returns:**
  A new Song with audio_bytes populated.

Example:

```default
updated = arioso.check_status(song)
if updated[0].status == "complete":
    song_with_audio = arioso.fetch_audio(updated[0])
    # song_with_audio.audio_bytes is now the raw MP3 data
```

### arioso.generate(prompt, , platform='musicgen', \*\*kwargs)

Generate music using the specified platform.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description of desired music.
  * **platform** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Name of the generation platform (default: ‘musicgen’).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Parameters using unified affordance names.
    See `arioso.base.AFFORDANCES` for the full list.
* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)
* **Returns:**
  A Song object containing the generated audio and metadata.

Example:

```default
song = generate("upbeat jazz piano", platform="musicgen", duration=10)
```

### arioso.generate_many(prompt, , platform='musicgen', \*\*kwargs)

Generate music, returning all results (some platforms return multiple).

Same interface as [`generate()`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.generate) but always returns a list.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)]

  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### arioso.list_platforms()

Return names of all available platforms.

### arioso.platform_table(, fields=('name', 'access_type', 'weights_license', 'commercial_use'))

One row per platform: its access type, weights licence and commercial use.

Reads the platforms’ configs only, so no adapter (and no optional dependency)
is loaded. `commercial_use` is one of `COMMERCIAL_USE_VALUES`.

* **Parameters:**
  **fields** – The config keys each row carries (a missing key reads `None`).
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]
* **Returns:**
  A list of dicts, one per platform, keyed by `fields`.

Example:

```default
free = [r["name"] for r in arioso.platform_table() if r["commercial_use"] == "yes"]
```

### arioso.supports_audio_input(platform)

Whether *platform* can condition on caller-supplied input audio.

Returns True if the platform declares any of
[`AUDIO_INPUT_AFFORDANCES`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.AUDIO_INPUT_AFFORDANCES) (`audio_input` / `melody` /
`reference_audio`) in its config’s `supported_affordances`.

Example:

```default
arioso.supports_audio_input("stable_audio")  # True
arioso.supports_audio_input("mubert")        # False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

# _autosummary/arioso.named_prompts.html.md

# arioso.named_prompts

Named prompts: a ledger of (name, prompt_text) pairs organized by category.

Provides a system for looking up sonic descriptions by name (artist, mood, genre,
instrument, etc.) to help users craft prompts for AI music generation without using
restricted names.

The system has two layers:

- **Starter data**: ships with arioso in `arioso/data/named_prompts/*.yaml`
- **User data**: stored in `~/.local/share/arioso/named_prompts/*.yaml`

User data overlays starter data, so users can extend or override entries.

Usage:

```default
>>> from arioso.named_prompts import named_prompts, search
>>> named_prompts.artists['billie_eilish']  # attribute access by category
'...'
>>> named_prompts['artists', 'billie_eilish']  # flat key access
'...'
>>> results = search('jazz')  # search across all categories
```

### Functions

| [`add_prompt`](_autosummary/arioso.named_prompts.html.md#arioso.named_prompts.add_prompt)(category, name, prompt_text, \*[, ...])   | Add or update a prompt in the user's data.               |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| [`get_named_prompts`](_autosummary/arioso.named_prompts.html.md#arioso.named_prompts.get_named_prompts)()                                  | Return a module-level singleton `NamedPrompts` instance. |
| [`remove_prompt`](_autosummary/arioso.named_prompts.html.md#arioso.named_prompts.remove_prompt)(category, name)                        | Remove a prompt from the user's data.                    |
| [`search`](_autosummary/arioso.named_prompts.html.md#arioso.named_prompts.search)(query, \*[, categories, ...])                 | Search for prompts matching a query string.              |

### Classes

| [`NamedPrompts`](_autosummary/arioso.named_prompts.html.md#arioso.named_prompts.NamedPrompts)(\*[, include_user_data])   | Two-level mapping of `(category, name) -> prompt_text`.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.named_prompts.NamedPrompts(, include_user_data=True)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)

Two-level mapping of `(category, name) -> prompt_text`.

Supports both hierarchical and flat access:

```default
np = NamedPrompts()
np.artists['billie_eilish']     # attribute access to a category
np['artists']['billie_eilish']  # dict-style
np['artists', 'billie_eilish']  # flat tuple key
```

Categories are auto-discovered from YAML files in the starter and user dirs.

* **Parameters:**
  **include_user_data** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to layer user data on top of starter data.
  Defaults to `True`.

#### *property* categories *: [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]*

Return all available category names.

#### flat()

Return a flat dict of `{(category, name): prompt_text}`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### flat_names(, warn_collisions=True)

Return a flat dict of `{name: prompt_text}`, ignoring categories.

If the same name appears in multiple categories, the last one wins
and a warning is issued (unless `warn_collisions=False`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### arioso.named_prompts.add_prompt(category, name, prompt_text, , confirm_override=True)

Add or update a prompt in the user’s data.

If the name already exists in either user or starter data and
`confirm_override` is True, a confirmation prompt is printed on the
first collision.

* **Parameters:**
  * **category** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The category to add to (e.g. ‘artists’, ‘moods’).
  * **name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The identifier for this prompt.
  * **prompt_text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The sonic description / prompt text.
  * **confirm_override** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, warn when overriding an existing entry.
* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### arioso.named_prompts.get_named_prompts()

Return a module-level singleton `NamedPrompts` instance.

* **Return type:**
  [`NamedPrompts`](_autosummary/arioso.named_prompts.html.md#arioso.named_prompts.NamedPrompts)

### arioso.named_prompts.remove_prompt(category, name)

Remove a prompt from the user’s data.

This only removes from user data. Starter data entries cannot be removed
(but can be overridden via `add_prompt`).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### arioso.named_prompts.search(query, , categories=None, search_prompts=True, search_names=True)

Search for prompts matching a query string.

* **Parameters:**
  * **query** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Case-insensitive substring to search for.
  * **categories** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]]) – If given, restrict search to these categories.
  * **search_prompts** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to search in prompt text.
  * **search_names** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to search in entry names.
* **Return type:**
  [`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]
* **Returns:**
  Dict of `{(category, name): prompt_text}` for all matches.


# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.ace_step.adapter.html.md

# arioso.platforms.ace_step.adapter

ACE-Step adapter: fal.ai’s hosted endpoint, or ACE-Step 1.5 run locally.

`runtime="fal"` (the default) is the config-driven `arioso._fal.FalAdapter` (the
mapping lives in this platform’s `config.py`); `runtime="local"` runs ACE-Step 1.5 in
its own environment (`arioso.platforms.ace_step._local`). `$ARIOSO_ACE_STEP_RUNTIME`
changes the default, e.g. to `local` on a machine with the runtime installed. The module-level `fal_run` /
`fal_upload_audio` are looked up at call time, so tests can patch them here.

### Module Attributes

| [`LOCAL_ONLY`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.ace_step.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.ace_step.adapter.LOCAL_ONLY)   | Keywords only the local runtime understands (fal's endpoint has no such controls).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.ace_step.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.ace_step.adapter.Adapter)([config, local])   | ACE-Step adapter (fal.ai hosted, or local ACE-Step 1.5).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.platforms.ace_step.adapter.Adapter(config=None, , local=None)

Bases: `FalAdapter`

ACE-Step adapter (fal.ai hosted, or local ACE-Step 1.5).

#### accepted_params()

fal’s keywords plus the local runtime’s own controls and `runtime` itself.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)

#### generate(prompt='', , runtime=None, \*\*params)

Generate with fal or locally; see the module docstring for how `runtime` resolves.

#### *property* local *: LocalAceStep*

The local runtime (built on first use; its worker starts on the first call).

### arioso.platforms.ace_step.adapter.LOCAL_ONLY *= ('bpm', 'key', 'model', 'lm_model', 'audio_input_strength', 'reference_audio', 'timesignature')*

# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.beatoven.adapter.html.md

# arioso.platforms.beatoven.adapter

Beatoven.ai adapter via REST API.

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.beatoven.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.beatoven.adapter.Adapter)(config)   | Adapter for Beatoven.ai music generation.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.platforms.beatoven.adapter.Adapter(config)

Bases: `BaseRestAdapter`

Adapter for Beatoven.ai music generation.

Beatoven uses a three-step flow:

1. POST /tracks to create a track and get a track_id.
2. Poll GET /tracks/{track_id} until status is ‘composed’.
3. GET /tracks/{track_id}/audio to retrieve the download URL.

#### generate(prompt, , duration=30, negative_prompt='', seed=None, guidance=16, num_steps=100, looping=False, wait_for_completion=True, poll_interval=5.0, timeout=300.0, \*\*kwargs)

Generate music via Beatoven.ai.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description of desired music.
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Track duration in seconds (5-150).
  * **negative_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Elements to avoid in generation.
  * **seed** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Random seed for reproducibility.
  * **guidance** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Creativity/guidance scale (default 16).
  * **num_steps** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Refinement steps (default 100).
  * **looping** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to generate loopable audio.
  * **wait_for_completion** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, poll until audio is ready.
  * **poll_interval** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds between status checks.
  * **timeout** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Max seconds to wait for completion.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)]
* **Returns:**
  List containing a single Song object.

#### get_audio_url(track_id)

Retrieve the audio download URL for a completed track.

* **Parameters:**
  **track_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The track ID of a composed track.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Returns:**
  The audio download URL.

#### get_status(track_id)

Check the generation status of a track.

* **Parameters:**
  **track_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The track ID returned from generate().
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Returns:**
  Status string from the API (e.g. ‘composing’, ‘composed’).
