# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md

# arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter

Foundation-1 adapter: stable-audio-tools in its own environment, one worker per adapter.

The model loads once, in a `Worker` running
`arioso/_workers/foundation_1_worker.py` with the Python of the `foundation-1`
environment, which `ensure_env()` builds on first use (pinned
stable-audio-tools, torch 2.7). `make_worker=` and `ensure_env=` are the seams.

Foundation-1 reads a tag prompt: instrument family and sub-family, timbre, notation and FX
tags, then `"<N> Bars, <BPM> BPM, <key>"` (see [`build_prompt()`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.build_prompt)). arioso’s `bpm`
and `key` become those tags; a loop’s length follows from its bars and tempo, so with a
tempo the clip is exactly `bars` bars of 4/4 (`bars=` 4 or 8, else the count nearest
to `duration`). Without one, `duration` is the clip length (a one-shot or free clip).

### Module Attributes

| [`BEATS_PER_BAR`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.BEATS_PER_BAR)     | Beats in a bar (the loops are 4/4).                                                                                                         |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`WINDOW_SECONDS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.WINDOW_SECONDS)    | Seconds of audio the model renders at most (its 882000-sample window at 44.1 kHz).                                                          |
| [`DFLT_SAMPLER`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.DFLT_SAMPLER)      | stable-audio-tools' sampler and noise schedule used for Stable Audio Open 1.0.                                                              |
| [`WORKER_ENV`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.WORKER_ENV)        | MPS falls back to the CPU for an operator it lacks.                                                                                         |
| [`TARGET_NOTE_TAG`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.TARGET_NOTE_TAG)   | The tag before a one-shot's pitch, and the keybeds checkpoint's single-note prefix (`keybed_training_strategy.md` in the model repository). |
| [`DFLT_NOTE_SECONDS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.DFLT_NOTE_SECONDS) | A one-shot's length when no duration is given (the keybed notes were trained at 3 s).                                                       |

### Functions

| [`build_prompt`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.build_prompt)(prompt, \*[, bpm, key, bars, ...])   | The tag prompt, the clip's seconds and the timing it used, from arioso's controls.    |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`cached_weights`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.cached_weights)([model, config])                   | The local path of `model`'s checkpoint in the Hugging Face cache, or None if absent.  |
| [`hf_hub_cache`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.hf_hub_cache)()                                    | The Hugging Face hub cache: `$HF_HUB_CACHE`, else `$HF_HOME/hub`, else the default.   |
| [`normalize_key`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.normalize_key)(key)                                | A key as Foundation-1's tags spell it: `"Am"` -> `"A minor"`, `"f#"` -> `"F# major"`. |
| [`normalize_note`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.normalize_note)(note)                              | A pitch as the tags spell it (`"c#3"` -> `"C#3"`); a ValueError if it is not one.     |
| [`parse_key`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.parse_key)(key)                                    | `(spelling, pitch_class, mode)` of a key, or None if `key` is not one.                |

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.Adapter)([config, make_worker, ensure_env, ...])   | Local Foundation-1 adapter (stable-audio-tools, MPS / CUDA / CPU).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.Adapter(config=None, \*, make_worker=<class 'ps.isolated.Worker'>, ensure_env=<function ensure_env>, is_supported=<function \_is_supported>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Local Foundation-1 adapter (stable-audio-tools, MPS / CUDA / CPU).

#### close()

Stop the worker (the loaded model is released).

#### generate(prompt, , duration=None, bpm=None, key=None, bars=None, note=None, model='foundation-1', num_steps=100, guidance=7.0, seed=None, negative_prompt=None, sampler='dpmpp-3m-sde', device=None, normalize=True, \*\*kwargs)

Render a loop or a one-shot for the tag prompt `prompt`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Foundation-1 tags, e.g. `"Synth Lead, Warm, Arp, Medium Reverb"`
    (instrument, timbre, notation, FX; see the model card). Passed through,
    with the bar, tempo and key tags appended when given as arguments.
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds; without a tempo, the clip length (default 10), with one,
    only the hint for the bar count.
  * **bpm** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Tempo, appended as `"<bpm> BPM"` (trained on 100-150, see the config).
  * **key** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Key, appended as e.g. `"E minor"` (`"Em"` and `"E minor"` both work).
  * **bars** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – 4 or 8, with a tempo: the loop is exactly that many 4/4 bars.
  * **note** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A one-shot’s pitch (`"C3"`), appended as `"Target Note, C3"`; with
    `model="1.2-keybeds"` the prompt takes that checkpoint’s single-note
    form (`"Keybed, Timbre Profile, ..."`). Default length 3 s.
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"foundation-1"` (loops), `"1.2-samples"` (loops and one-shots) or
    `"1.2-keybeds"` (pitch-consistent one-shots).
  * **num_steps** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Sampler steps.
  * **guidance** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – CFG scale.
  * **seed** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Seed; a fresh one is drawn and recorded when None.
  * **negative_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What to steer away from.
  * **sampler** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – stable-audio-tools sampler type.
  * **device** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"mps"`, `"cuda"` or `"cpu"`; default: the best available.
  * **normalize** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Scale the take to full scale (its peak at 0 dBFS). `False`
    keeps the model’s own level (written as float, so nothing clips): takes
    meant to sit side by side, such as a keybed’s chunks, keep their balance.
* **Returns:**
  A complete Song (44.1 kHz stereo wav), the prompt sent in its metadata.

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.BEATS_PER_BAR *= 4*

Beats in a bar (the loops are 4/4).

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.DFLT_NOTE_SECONDS *= 3.0*

A one-shot’s length when no duration is given (the keybed notes were trained at 3 s).

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.DFLT_SAMPLER *= 'dpmpp-3m-sde'*

stable-audio-tools’ sampler and noise schedule used for Stable Audio Open 1.0.

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.TARGET_NOTE_TAG *= 'Target Note'*

The tag before a one-shot’s pitch, and the keybeds checkpoint’s single-note prefix
(`keybed_training_strategy.md` in the model repository).

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.WINDOW_SECONDS *= 20.0*

Seconds of audio the model renders at most (its 882000-sample window at 44.1 kHz).

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.WORKER_ENV *= {'PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK': '1', 'TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM': 'false'}*

MPS falls back to the CPU for an operator it lacks.

* **Type:**
  Variables for the worker

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.build_prompt(prompt, , bpm=None, key=None, bars=None, duration=None, note=None, keybed=False, supported_bars=(4, 8))

The tag prompt, the clip’s seconds and the timing it used, from arioso’s controls.

Tags already in `prompt` are read and must agree with the arguments (`"140 BPM"`
with `bpm=120` is an error; keys compare by pitch class and mode, so `"Cb major"`
agrees with `"B major"`); a short key tag (`"Am"`) is spelt out. Missing tags go
in the model card’s order, `..., 8 Bars, 140 BPM, E minor`: bars before the tempo
(also when only the tempo was in the prompt), the key last.

With a tempo (`bpm` or a `BPM` tag) the clip is `bars` bars of 4/4: `bars`,
else a `Bars` tag, else the supported count nearest to `duration * bpm / 240` (4
without a duration); a `duration` more than a bar away from that warns. Without a
tempo the clip is `duration` seconds (default 10).

`note` makes a one-shot at that pitch: `"Target Note, <note>"` is appended (no
tempo or bars then; default length 3 s; a key goes before it; a `Target Note` already
in the prompt is read like the other tags), and with `keybed=True` (the keybeds
checkpoint) the prompt starts with its single-note prefix `"Keybed, Timbre Profile"`.

```pycon
>>> build_prompt("Synth Lead, Warm, Arp", bpm=140, key="Em", duration=12)
('Synth Lead, Warm, Arp, 8 Bars, 140 BPM, E minor', 13.714285714285714, {'bpm': 140, 'bars': 8, 'key': 'E minor', 'note': None})
>>> build_prompt("Grand Piano, Bright", note="c3", keybed=True)[:2]
('Keybed, Timbre Profile, Grand Piano, Bright, Target Note, C3', 3.0)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.cached_weights(model='foundation-1', , config=None)

The local path of `model`’s checkpoint in the Hugging Face cache, or None if absent.

Looks at the pinned revision only (no network, no huggingface_hub import).

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.hf_hub_cache()

The Hugging Face hub cache: `$HF_HUB_CACHE`, else `$HF_HOME/hub`, else the default.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.normalize_key(key)

A key as Foundation-1’s tags spell it: `"Am"` -> `"A minor"`, `"f#"` -> `"F# major"`.

Anything that is not a key comes back stripped, unchanged.

```pycon
>>> normalize_key("Am"), normalize_key("C# minor"), normalize_key("eb")
('A minor', 'C# minor', 'Eb major')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.normalize_note(note)

A pitch as the tags spell it (`"c#3"` -> `"C#3"`); a ValueError if it is not one.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.adapter.parse_key(key)

`(spelling, pitch_class, mode)` of a key, or None if `key` is not one.

The spelling is the tags’ (`"A minor"`); the pitch class compares enharmonics.

```pycon
>>> parse_key("Am"), parse_key("f# major"), parse_key("Bell")
(('A minor', 9, 'minor'), ('F# major', 6, 'major'), None)
```


# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.html.md

# arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config

Foundation-1 platform configuration (local, stable-audio-tools in its own environment).

Foundation-1 (`RoyalCities/Foundation-1` on the Hugging Face Hub, ungated) is a fine-tune
of Stable Audio Open 1.0 for structured, tempo- and bar-aware instrument loops and
one-shots: one `model_config.json` (a stable-audio-tools `diffusion_cond` model: oobleck
VAE, T5-base prompt encoder, `seconds_start`/`seconds_total`, DiT; 44.1 kHz stereo, a
20 s window) shared by three checkpoints. Weights: Stability AI Community License (free
for research and non-commercial use, commercial use below US$1M annual revenue). Verified
against the model card, `Master_Tag_Reference.md` and `model_config.json` at the
revision below on 2026-11-10.

stable-audio-tools pins its own torch and Python (`<3.11`), so it runs in an environment
arioso builds once with `uv` (`EnvSpec`, under
`~/.local/share/arioso/envs/foundation-1`; `$ARIOSO_FOUNDATION_1_ENV` names an existing
environment instead); weights go to the Hugging Face cache. torch 2.7 has no Intel macOS
wheels, so on a Mac it needs Apple Silicon.

### Module Attributes

| [`SUPPORTED_BARS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.SUPPORTED_BARS)   | bar counts and tempos the loops were trained on.                                                                                                                     |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`RESOLVED_ON`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.RESOLVED_ON)      | uv ignores anything published later, so the packages left unpinned below resolve to the same versions on every machine.                                              |
| [`REQUIREMENTS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.REQUIREMENTS)     | stable-audio-tools and the packages whose versions decide its behaviour, pinned (the set resolved on RESOLVED_ON); the rest follow from these and `--exclude-newer`. |
| [`T5`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.T5)               | the worker fetches these files at this revision and points the conditioner at them, so nothing is looked up online once they are cached.                             |

### Functions

| [`env_spec`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.html.md#arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.env_spec)([system])   | The environment for `system` (`platform.system()` by default).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.REQUIREMENTS *= ('stable-audio-tools==0.0.20', 'torch==2.7.1', 'torchaudio==2.7.1', 'transformers==4.57.1', 'tokenizers==0.22.1', 'huggingface-hub==0.36.0', 'safetensors==0.6.2', 'numpy==1.26.4', 'scipy==1.15.3', 'sentencepiece==0.1.99', 'torchsde==0.2.6', 'soundfile==0.13.1', 'pytorch-lightning==2.5.5', '--exclude-newer=2026-11-10T00:00:00Z')*

stable-audio-tools and the packages whose versions decide its behaviour, pinned (the
set resolved on RESOLVED_ON); the rest follow from these and `--exclude-newer`.

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.RESOLVED_ON *= '2026-11-10'*

uv ignores anything published later, so
the packages left unpinned below resolve to the same versions on every machine.

* **Type:**
  The date the requirements were resolved on

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.SUPPORTED_BARS *= (4, 8)*

bar counts and tempos the loops were trained on.

* **Type:**
  The model card’s prompt grammar

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.T5 *= {'files': ('config.json', 'generation_config.json', 'model.safetensors', 'spiece.model', 'tokenizer.json'), 'repo_id': 'google-t5/t5-base', 'revision': 'a9723ea7f1b39c1eae772870f3b547bf6ef7e6c1'}*

the worker
fetches these files at this revision and points the conditioner at them, so nothing
is looked up online once they are cached.

* **Type:**
  The T5-base text encoder the model’s prompt conditioner loads, pinned

### arioso.platforms.foundation_1.config.env_spec(system=None)

The environment for `system` (`platform.system()` by default).

On Linux uv picks the torch wheel matching the machine’s accelerator (CUDA or CPU)
instead of PyPI’s default CUDA build; macOS wheels carry MPS, there is no index to pick.

* **Return type:**
  `EnvSpec`

#### generate(prompt, , negative_prompt='', seed=None, model='lyria-002', batch_size=1, \*\*kwargs)

Generate music using Google Lyria 2.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description of desired music.
  * **negative_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Elements to avoid in the generation.

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Lyria RealTime adapter using streaming music sessions.

Creates a live music session via the `google-genai` SDK, sends a
prompt, collects PCM audio chunks for a configurable duration, and
returns them as a single `Song`.

#### generate(prompt, , duration=10.0, bpm=None, key=None, energy=None, brightness=None, guidance=4.0, temperature=1.1, top_k=40, seed=None, prompt_weight=None, \*\*kwargs)

Generate music using a Lyria RealTime streaming session.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description of desired music.
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds of audio to collect from the stream.
  * **bpm** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Beats per minute (60-200).

  * **brightness** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Spectral brightness (0-1).
  * **guidance** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Guidance strength (0-6).
  * **temperature** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Sampling temperature (0-3).
  * **top_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Top-k sampling (1-1000).
  * **seed** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Random seed for reproducibility (0-2.1B).
  * **prompt_weight** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Weight applied to the WeightedPrompt.

  [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)

# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.magenta_rt.adapter.html.md

# arioso.platforms.magenta_rt.adapter

Magenta RealTime 2 adapter: offline renders from a worker in magenta-rt’s own environment.

The model loads once, in a `Worker` running
`arioso/_workers/magenta_rt_worker.py` with the runtime’s Python (MLX pinned below 0.32, which arioso’s environment
need not share). Style comes from the text `prompt` or a `reference_audio` clip; there
is no tempo control beyond the words, and no seed (the sampler is not seedable).

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.magenta_rt.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.magenta_rt.adapter.Adapter)([config, make_worker])   | Local Magenta RealTime 2 (MLX) adapter.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|

Local Magenta RealTime 2 (MLX) adapter.

#### close()

Stop the worker (the loaded model is released).

#### generate(prompt, , duration=10.0, model='mrt2_small', temperature=1.3, top_k=40, guidance=3.0, reference_audio=None, \*\*kwargs)

Render `duration` seconds in the style of `prompt` (or of `reference_audio`).

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Style text (genre, instruments, mood; tempo only as words).
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds of audio (25 frames a second).
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"mrt2_small"` (real time on M1-class Macs) or `"mrt2_base"`.
  * **temperature** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Sampling temperature.
  * **top_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Top-k sampling.
  * **guidance** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – CFG scale on the style embedding.
  * **reference_audio** – A clip whose style replaces the text prompt’s.

# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.magenta_rt.config.html.md

# arioso.platforms.magenta_rt.config

Magenta RealTime 2 platform configuration (local MLX runtime, Apple Silicon).

`magenta-rt[mlx]` (Apache-2.0 code) with the exported `.mlxfn` models; weights
CC-BY-4.0 (Google claims no rights in generated outputs). `mlx<0.32` is pinned because
MLX 0.32 cannot load the exported functions (magenta/magenta-realtime#103). Verified
against `magenta_rt/mlx/generate.py` of magenta-rt on 2026-11-10. Offline renders only:
the streaming state is not exposed yet.

# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.html.md

# arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter

MusicGen adapter using MLX (text, Apple Silicon), audiocraft or transformers.

The adapter holds the modes; `backends.py` holds how each library runs them.

Supports text-to-music generation and, via `facebook/musicgen-melody`,
melody-conditioned generation (the `melody` affordance / `arioso.enhance`
stage): the output follows the pitch contour of an input audio while taking its
style from the text prompt.

It also *continues* a recording (the `continue_from` affordance): the last
`prompt_seconds` of the audio are fed to the model as an audio prompt and it
generates what comes next, chained over `rounds` calls for longer extensions.
This is the local fallback for extending audio that a hosted extend route
refuses (`sunoapi.upload_extend` rejects uploads matching a catalogued
composition; thorwhalen/arioso#29).

### Module Attributes

| [`WINDOW_SECONDS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.WINDOW_SECONDS)         | an audio prompt plus the new audio it generates must fit in it (transformers caps generation at 1500 frames).                                         |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SEAM_CROSSFADE_SECONDS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.SEAM_CROSSFADE_SECONDS) | Crossfade from the original audio into the model's re-decoded prompt at each seam, hiding the codec's reconstruction error there (a click otherwise). |

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.Adapter)(config, \*[, backend_for, load_backend])   | MusicGen adapter with lazy model loading.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.Adapter(config, , backend_for=None, load_backend=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

MusicGen adapter with lazy model loading.

`backend_for` (model variant -> backend class) chooses the library without
loading weights (`select_backend_class()`: MLX for text takes on Apple Silicon when
its runtime is installed, else `audiocraft` when it imports, else `transformers`);
a chooser that takes a `task` keyword is told the task. The chosen class is
asked what it can do (`can_continue`) and then loads the weights, so the class
that answers is the class that loads. `load_backend` (model variant ->
`Backend`) replaces the choice and the loading together: nothing is asked
before it loads, and the backend it returns is on its own.

#### generate(prompt, , duration=8.0, temperature=1.0, top_k=250, top_p=0.0, guidance=3.0, model='facebook/musicgen-small', melody=None, continue_from=None, continue_at=None, prompt_seconds=10.0, extend_seconds=None, rounds=1, \*\*kwargs)

Generate music from a text prompt, optionally following a melody or
continuing a recording.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description of desired music.
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Length in seconds.
  * **temperature** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Sampling randomness.
  * **top_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Top-k sampling parameter.
  * **top_p** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Top-p nucleus sampling.
  * **guidance** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Classifier-free guidance scale.
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Model variant name (e.g. ‘facebook/musicgen-small’). When a
    `melody` is supplied and `model` isn’t already a melody
    variant, it is switched to `facebook/musicgen-melody`.
  * **melody** – Optional input audio whose pitch contour the output follows
    (a Song/AudioResult/bytes/path/(array, sample_rate)/waveform).
    This is the `arioso.enhance` path for musicgen.
  * **continue_from** – Optional audio to extend, in any of the forms
    `melody` accepts. The result is this audio followed by its
    continuation (mono, at the model’s sample rate); the
    continuation alone is in `metadata['continuation']`. Each
    seam crossfades over 10 ms into the model’s re-decoded prompt,
    so join the result, not the original plus the continuation.
  * **continue_at** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Continue from this time (seconds) in
    `continue_from` instead of from its end; what follows it is
    dropped.
  * **prompt_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Length of the tail of the audio fed to the model as
    the prompt for each round.
  * **extend_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – New audio per round, in seconds (default
    `duration`). `prompt_seconds + extend_seconds` must fit in
    [`WINDOW_SECONDS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.WINDOW_SECONDS).
  * **rounds** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Number of chained continuation calls, each prompted by the
    tail of the audio so far, so the extension totals
    `rounds * extend_seconds`.
* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)
* **Returns:**
  A Song with audio_array populated.

### arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.SEAM_CROSSFADE_SECONDS *= 0.01*

Crossfade from the original audio into the model’s re-decoded prompt at each
seam, hiding the codec’s reconstruction error there (a click otherwise).

### arioso.platforms.musicgen.adapter.WINDOW_SECONDS *= 30.0*

an audio prompt plus the new audio it
generates must fit in it (transformers caps generation at 1500 frames).

* **Type:**
  MusicGen’s context window in seconds


# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.html.md

# arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends

The ways to run MusicGen, behind one interface (thorwhalen/arioso#31, #54).

The adapter holds the modes (text, melody, continuation: window checks, chaining, splicing); a
backend holds what one library needs to load a model and run it in each of them. `audiocraft`
is Meta’s library, `transformers` the HuggingFace port, and `mlx` Apple’s MLX port
(`ml-explore/mlx-examples`), which runs in its own environment through a worker and only
does text. Each backend wraps a model that is already loaded, so building one is free;
`load` is what loads one.

Which one runs ([`select_backend_class()`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.select_backend_class)): `$ARIOSO_MUSICGEN_BACKEND` when set; else
MLX for a text take on Apple Silicon when its runtime is installed; else audiocraft when it
imports; else transformers. On Apple Silicon, transformers runs on the CPU unless
`$ARIOSO_TORCH_DEVICE` says otherwise: on MPS it was 15-30x slower and grew Metal memory
on every decoding step (42 GB after three 10 s clips on an M1 Max).

audiocraft and transformers return the model’s own layout for text and melody,
`(channels, frames)` from audiocraft and `(frames,)` from transformers’ first channel, and
mono for a continuation; MLX returns `(frames,)`.

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_FRAME_RATE`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.DEFAULT_FRAME_RATE)   | Codec frames per second, used when a model does not report its own.                   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`BACKEND_ENV_VAR`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.BACKEND_ENV_VAR)      | `audiocraft`, `transformers` or `mlx`.                                                |
| [`MLX_MAX_SECONDS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.MLX_MAX_SECONDS)      | MusicGen's context in seconds (1500 frames); the MLX port does not stop there itself. |
| [`MLX_CHECKPOINTS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.MLX_CHECKPOINTS)      | The checkpoints the MLX port loads.                                                   |
| [`TASKS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.TASKS)                | plain text, follow a melody, or continue audio.                                       |
| [`BACKENDS`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.html.md#arioso.platforms.musicgen.backends.BACKENDS)             | The backends by the name `$ARIOSO_MUSICGEN_BACKEND` takes.                            |

### Functions

# arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter

Stable Audio Open adapter using HuggingFace Diffusers.

Runs on `arioso._util.torch_device()` (CUDA, else Apple MPS, else CPU), in
float16 on CUDA only. The Stability AI repositories are gated: accept the
licence on the model’s Hugging Face page and log in before the first load.

### Module Attributes

| [`SEED_BOUND`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.SEED_BOUND)   | Seeds are drawn below this bound when none is given, so every take records one.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`load_pipeline`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.load_pipeline)(model)               | `diffusers.StableAudioPipeline` for *model*, on the shared torch device.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_torch_generator`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.make_torch_generator)(device, seed) | A `torch.Generator` on *device* seeded with *seed*.                        |

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.Adapter)(config, \*[, load_pipeline, ...])   | Stable Audio Open adapter with lazy model loading.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.Adapter(config, \*, load_pipeline=<function load_pipeline>, make_generator=<function make_torch_generator>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Stable Audio Open adapter with lazy model loading.

Uses `diffusers.StableAudioPipeline` for local inference. `load_pipeline`
(model id -> pipeline) and `make_generator` ((device, seed) -> generator)
are the seams that keep tests free of torch, diffusers and the gated weights.

#### generate(prompt, , negative_prompt=None, duration=10.0, num_steps=200, guidance=7.0, seed=None, batch_size=1, sampler='dpmpp-3m-sde', audio_input=None, audio_input_strength=None, model='stabilityai/stable-audio-open-1.0', \*\*kwargs)

Generate audio from a text prompt, optionally conditioned on input audio.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description of desired audio.
  * **negative_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description of undesired characteristics.
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Length in seconds.
  * **num_steps** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Number of diffusion inference steps.
  * **guidance** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Classifier-free guidance scale.
  * **seed** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Random seed for reproducibility. When omitted, one is drawn
    and recorded in `metadata['seed']`, so every take can be redone.
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Number of waveforms to generate.
  * **sampler** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Sampler type for the diffusion process.
  * **audio_input** – Optional input audio to condition on (audio-to-audio):
    a Song/AudioResult/bytes/path/(array, sample_rate)/NumPy waveform.
    Passed to the pipeline as `initial_audio_waveforms` – i.e. the
    model continues/initializes from this audio.
  * **audio_input_strength** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Accepted for API symmetry but **ignored** –
    the diffusers `StableAudioPipeline` exposes no denoise/strength
    control (that is a stable-audio-tools/ComfyUI feature). A warning
    is emitted if a value is passed alongside `audio_input`.
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Hugging Face id of a Stable Audio checkpoint that
    `StableAudioPipeline` loads.
* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)
* **Returns:**
  A Song with audio_array populated.

### arioso.platforms.stable_audio.adapter.SEED_BOUND *= 2147483648*

Seeds are drawn below this bound when none is given, so every take records one.

`diffusers.StableAudioPipeline` for *model*, on the shared torch device.

# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.stable_audio_3.adapter.html.md

# arioso.platforms.stable_audio_3.adapter

Stable Audio 3 adapter: Stability’s pure-MLX build, run as one process per take.

The MLX build is a script in the `Stability-AI/stable-audio-3` checkout with its own
virtualenv (see the config’s `runtime`), so each call runs `scripts/sa3_mlx.py` there
(the small model loads in about a second, so a persistent worker would buy little) and
reads back the wav it wrote. A seed is always passed and recorded (a fresh one when none
is given). `runner=` is the process seam.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_A2A_NOISE`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.stable_audio_3.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.stable_audio_3.adapter.DFLT_A2A_NOISE)   | Noise level for audio-to-audio when none is given; inpainting starts from pure noise (1.0).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.stable_audio_3.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.stable_audio_3.adapter.Adapter)([config, runner, is_supported])   | Local Stable Audio 3 (MLX) adapter.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.platforms.stable_audio_3.adapter.Adapter(config=None, \*, runner=<function run_process>, is_supported=<function is_apple_silicon>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Local Stable Audio 3 (MLX) adapter.

#### generate(prompt, , duration=10.0, model='sm-music', num_steps=8, guidance=1.0, seed=None, negative_prompt=None, audio_input=None, audio_input_strength=None, inpaint_range=None, timeout=None, \*\*kwargs)

Generate `duration` seconds for `prompt`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Text description (tempo and key only through the text, e.g. “100 BPM”).
  * **duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds of audio (trimmed exactly).
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"sm-music"` (fast), `"sm-sfx"` (sound effects) or `"medium"`.
  * **num_steps** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Sampler steps (the models are distilled for 8).
  * **guidance** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – CFG scale; 1.0 (the default) runs no unconditional branch, so a
    `negative_prompt` acts only above 1.
  * **seed** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Seed; a fresh one is drawn and recorded when None.
  * **negative_prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What to steer away from (needs `guidance` above 1).
  * **audio_input** – Audio to vary (audio-to-audio) or, with `inpaint_range`, to inpaint.
  * **audio_input_strength** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Noise level 0-1 applied to `audio_input` (higher = freer);
    default 0.7 for a variation, 1.0 for inpainting (which starts from noise).
  * **inpaint_range** – `(start, end)` seconds of `audio_input` to regenerate.
  * **timeout** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Seconds before the process is killed.
* **Returns:**
  A complete Song (wav bytes, array when soundfile is installed, metadata).

### arioso.platforms.stable_audio_3.adapter.DFLT_A2A_NOISE *= 0.7*

Noise level for audio-to-audio when none is given; inpainting starts from pure noise (1.0).

# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.sunoapi.adapter.html.md

# arioso.platforms.sunoapi.adapter

Suno adapter via sunoapi.org REST API.

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.sunoapi.adapter.html.md#arioso.platforms.sunoapi.adapter.Adapter)(config, \*[, task_store])   | Adapter for Suno music generation via sunoapi.org.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.platforms.sunoapi.adapter.Adapter(config, , task_store=None)

Bases: `BaseRestAdapter`

Adapter for Suno music generation via sunoapi.org.

Handles the distinction between simple generation (prompt only)
and custom generation (with lyrics/style via customMode).

The sunoapi.org API is callback-based: it returns a taskId immediately
and POSTs results to your callBackUrl when generation completes.
A no-op placeholder callback URL is used by default, so polling via
`get_status()` (or `wait_for_completion=True`) works out of the box.
Set the SUNO_CALLBACK_URL env var to a real webhook if you want push
notifications.

After calling generate(), use get_status() to poll for results, or
use generate() with wait_for_completion=True to block until audio is ready.

All generation requests and status polls are automatically recorded in a
local task store (`SunoTasks`).  Access it via the `tasks` property:

```default
adapter = Adapter(config)
adapter.tasks                # SunoTasks Mapping
adapter.tasks.last(10)       # last 10 tasks
adapter.tasks.failed()       # all failed tasks
```

#### fetch_audio(song)

Download the audio bytes for a Song that has an audio_url.

* **Parameters:**
  **song** ([`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)) – A Song object with a populated audio_url.
* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)
* **Returns:**
  A new Song with audio_bytes populated.

#### get_status(task_id)

Check the status of a generation task and return updated Songs.

* **Parameters:**
  **task_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The taskId returned from generate(), upload_extend(),
  or upload_cover().
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song)]
* **Returns:**
  List of Song objects with current status and audio URLs
  (if generation is complete).

#### get_timestamped_lyrics(song_or_task_id, audio_id=None)

Suno’s own alignment of the sung lyric to a finished song.

One entry per sung *word* (Suno’s tokens: space-separated, so a whole
katakana word such as `バカンス` is one entry), in the order sung —
which can differ from the lyric you sent when Suno repeats or drops a
line. Times sit on a coarse (~0.16 s) grid and tend to run late, so
treat them as windows for a finer aligner rather than as onsets.

* **Parameters:**
  * **song_or_task_id** ([`Song`](_autosummary/arioso.base.html.md#arioso.base.Song) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – a completed `Song` from `get_status` /
    `poll_status` (it carries `metadata["task_id"]`), or a taskId.
  * **audio_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the song’s audio id; defaults to `song.id`.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)
* **Returns:**
  `{"aligned_words": [...], "hoot_cer": float | None, "raw": dict}`
  where each aligned word is `{"word", "text", "start", "end",
  "line_end", "section", "success"}`: `word` is Suno’s raw token
  (it may carry `[Section]` tags and newlines), `text` the token
  with those removed, `line_end` whether a lyric line ends there,
  `section` the label of a section starting at this word (else
  `None`). Bare section tags are folded onto the next word.
* **Raises:**
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – the Song is not complete, carries no task_id, or Suno
        has no alignment for it yet.
  * **hoot_cer\` is Suno's character error rate for the alignment** – 

#### *property* tasks

Local task store (`SunoTasks` Mapping) for recorded requests.

#### upload_file(file_path)

Upload a local audio file and return a public URL.

Uses the sunoapi.org file upload API. Uploaded files are temporary
and automatically deleted after 3 days.

* **Parameters:**
  **file_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Path to the local audio file.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Returns:**
  Public URL of the uploaded file.

# _autosummary/arioso.platforms.sunoapi.task_store.html.md

# arioso.platforms.sunoapi.task_store

Local task store for Suno API requests.

Provides a `collections.abc.Mapping` interface over locally-persisted task
records, so you can list, filter, and retrieve past Suno generation requests
without depending on a (non-existent) “list all” API endpoint.

Each task is stored as a JSON file keyed by `taskId`.  The store records
request parameters, status, timestamps, and the full API response.

Typical usage:

```default
from arioso.platforms.sunoapi.task_store import SunoTasks

tasks = SunoTasks()           # uses default data dir
tasks['5c79...be8e']          # get one task record
list(tasks)                   # all task IDs
len(tasks)                    # how many tasks

# Filtered views (return new Mapping objects):
tasks.last(20)                # last 20 by creation time
tasks.since(hours=24)         # created in last 24 hours
tasks.status('SUCCESS')       # only successful tasks
tasks.status('PENDING')       # only pending tasks
tasks.failed()                # all failed tasks
```

### Classes

| [`SunoTasks`](_autosummary/arioso.platforms.sunoapi.task_store.html.md#arioso.platforms.sunoapi.task_store.SunoTasks)([root_dir])   | A `Mapping[str, dict]` of Suno task records persisted as JSON files.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* arioso.platforms.sunoapi.task_store.SunoTasks(root_dir=None)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

A `Mapping[str, dict]` of Suno task records persisted as JSON files.

Keys are task IDs, values are task-record dicts with fields:

```default
task_id, operation, status, created_at, updated_at,
request_params, response
```

The store is backed by individual `.json` files in *root_dir*.

#### failed()

Return all tasks with an error status.

* **Return type:**
  `_FilteredTaskView`

#### last(n=20)

Return a view of the most recent *n* tasks (newest first).

* **Return type:**
  `_FilteredTaskView`

#### pending()

Return all tasks that are still pending or in progress.

* **Return type:**
  `_FilteredTaskView`

#### save(record)

Persist a task record (create or overwrite).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### since(, hours=0, minutes=0)

Return tasks created within the last *hours* + *minutes*.

* **Return type:**
  `_FilteredTaskView`

#### status(status_value)

Return tasks matching *status_value* (case-insensitive).

* **Return type:**
  `_FilteredTaskView`

#### succeeded()

Return all tasks that completed successfully.

* **Return type:**
  `_FilteredTaskView`

#### update(task_id, , status='', response=None)

Update an existing record’s status and/or response.

# _autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md

# arioso.schema

Machine-readable parameter schemas: what each platform accepts, as JSON Schema.

A front end, an agent or a form generator needs more than the parameter names: it
needs each parameter’s type, its bounds or choices, a display title and whether it
is shared across platforms. [`param_schema()`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.param_schema) assembles that from the two places
arioso already keeps it, so nothing is restated:

- **common** parameters are the unified affordances (`arioso.base.AFFORDANCES`)
  a platform lists in `supported_affordances`; their type, description and bounds
  come from the affordance, overridden by the platform’s `param_map` entry
  (`title`, `description`, `minimum`/`min`, `maximum`/`max`,
  `choices`, `default`, `type`).
- **extra** parameters are the platform’s own `adapter_params`. A platform may
  declare them as a dict of name to spec (the same keys as a `param_map` entry,
  `type` being a Python type); a bare list of names is still accepted, and such
  extras are marked `untyped` so a form can leave them out.

`native_default` is never used as a default: it is in the platform’s units
(milliseconds, a noise level), not the unified ones. A unified default is the
`default` key.

Example:

```default
>>> schema = param_schema("sunoapi")
>>> schema["properties"]["weirdness"]["x-arioso"]["group"]
'extra'
>>> schema["properties"]["audio_input_strength"]["maximum"]
1
```

### Module Attributes

| [`AUDIO_AFFORDANCES`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.AUDIO_AFFORDANCES)     | Affordances whose value is audio (a file, bytes, a waveform), not a scalar.                  |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`MECHANICS_AFFORDANCES`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.MECHANICS_AFFORDANCES) | Affordances that steer the call rather than the music; left out of schemas.                  |
| [`OPERATION_AFFORDANCES`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.OPERATION_AFFORDANCES) | Operations a platform supports, from the affordance that enables each.                       |
| [`MECHANICS_EXTRAS`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.MECHANICS_EXTRAS)      | Extras that steer the call (transport, process, device), not the music; left out of schemas. |

### Functions

| [`common_params`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.common_params)(platforms)   | The unified parameters every one of `platforms` supports, in the first one's order.                                                                                                                    |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`operations`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.operations)(config)         | What a platform can do, from its config: `generate` plus the operations its supported affordances enable (`cover` for `audio_input`, ...), or the config's own `operations` list when it declares one. |
| [`param_schema`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.param_schema)(platform)     | The JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the parameters `platform` accepts.                                                                                                                                  |
| [`schema_from_config`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.schema_from_config)(config) | The JSON Schema of a platform config (see [`param_schema()`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.param_schema)).                                                                                            |

### arioso.schema.AUDIO_AFFORDANCES *= frozenset({'audio_input', 'melody', 'reference_audio'})*

Affordances whose value is audio (a file, bytes, a waveform), not a scalar.

### arioso.schema.MECHANICS_AFFORDANCES *= frozenset({'wait_for_completion'})*

Affordances that steer the call rather than the music; left out of schemas.

### arioso.schema.MECHANICS_EXTRAS *= frozenset({'device', 'fetch', 'runtime', 'timeout'})*

Extras that steer the call (transport, process, device), not the music;
left out of schemas. A spec can also say `"mechanics": True`.

### arioso.schema.OPERATION_AFFORDANCES *= {'cover': 'audio_input', 'extend': 'continue_from', 'inpaint': 'mask_start', 'melody': 'melody', 'style_reference': 'reference_audio'}*

Operations a platform supports, from the affordance that enables each.

### arioso.schema.common_params(platforms)

The unified parameters every one of `platforms` supports, in the first one’s order.

Use it to lay out the part of a form that does not change when the user
switches platform.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### arioso.schema.operations(config)

What a platform can do, from its config: `generate` plus the operations its
supported affordances enable (`cover` for `audio_input`, …), or the
config’s own `operations` list when it declares one.

```pycon
>>> operations({"supported_affordances": ["prompt", "audio_input"]})
['generate', 'cover']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### arioso.schema.param_schema(platform)

The JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the parameters `platform` accepts.

Each property carries `x-arioso.group`: `"common"` for a unified
affordance (the same name on every platform that has it) or `"extra"` for a
parameter only this platform has. The schema’s own `x-arioso` lists both
groups and the platform’s `operations`. Reads the config only, so no adapter
or optional dependency is loaded.

* **Parameters:**
  **platform** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Platform identifier (see [`arioso.list_platforms()`](_autosummary/arioso.html.md#arioso.list_platforms)).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)
* **Returns:**
  A JSON-ready dict.

### arioso.schema.schema_from_config(config)

The JSON Schema of a platform config (see [`param_schema()`](_autosummary/arioso.schema.html.md#arioso.schema.param_schema)).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### arioso.tools.download_songs(songs, target_folder, , name_prefix='cover', adapter=None)

Download completed songs to *target_folder*. Returns list of saved paths.

### arioso.tools.ensure_adapter(adapter='sunoapi')

Return a ready-to-use platform adapter.

`adapter` can be:

- An existing adapter instance — returned as-is.
- A platform config dict — instantiated via its `Adapter` class.
- A string that is a valid platform name (e.g. `"sunoapi"`) — loaded
  from the arioso registry.
- `None` — falls back to `DFLT_PLATFORM`.

Raises `ValueError` for unrecognised inputs.

### arioso.tools.extract_style(filename)

Parse style from a filename like `barry_{key}_{bpm}bpm_{Style}.wav`.

### arioso.tools.poll_status(task_id, , poll_interval=15, timeout=600, adapter=None)

Poll until a task completes. Returns list of completed Song objects.

### arioso.tools.safe_name(text)

Convert arbitrary text to a filesystem-safe string.

### arioso.tools.submit_cover(source_path, \*, style='', prompt='', instrumental=True, model='V6', audio_weight=0.5, style_weight=0.5, source_prep=functools.partial(<function wav_to_mp3>, max_duration=480), adapter='sunoapi')

Submit an upload-cover job. Returns `(task_id, source_path)`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **source_path** – Path to source audio file.
  * **source_prep** – Callable `(path) -> path` to prepare the source file
    before upload (e.g. convert wav to mp3).  Defaults to
    [`wav_to_mp3()`](_autosummary/arioso.tools.html.md#arioso.tools.wav_to_mp3) (trimmed to *max_duration*).
  * **adapter** – Platform adapter, config dict, platform name, or `None`.

The caller is responsible for cleaning up *source_path* when done.

### arioso.tools.wav_to_mp3(wav_path, , max_duration=480)

Convert wav to a trimmed mp3. Returns path to a temp mp3 file.

The caller is responsible for deleting the temp file when done.


# _autosummary/arioso.translation.html.md

# arioso.translation

Parameter translation layer.

Translates between the unified affordance names and each platform’s
native parameter names, applying type coercions along the way.

### Module Attributes

| [`ALWAYS_RAISE_UNSUPPORTED`](_autosummary/arioso.translation.html.md#arioso.translation.ALWAYS_RAISE_UNSUPPORTED)   | Affordances that always raise on an unsupported platform, regardless of that platform's own `on_unsupported_param` policy.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`check_supported_params`](_autosummary/arioso.translation.html.md#arioso.translation.check_supported_params)(kwargs, config, \*[, ...])   | Warn or raise for kwargs not declared in a platform's `supported_affordances`.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_generate_func`](_autosummary/arioso.translation.html.md#arioso.translation.make_generate_func)(config)                          | Build a generate() callable from a platform config.                              |
| [`make_kwargs_trans`](_autosummary/arioso.translation.html.md#arioso.translation.make_kwargs_trans)(param_map, \*[, ...])             | Build a kwargs translation function from a platform's param_map.                 |

### arioso.translation.ALWAYS_RAISE_UNSUPPORTED *= ('lyrics',)*

Affordances that always raise on an unsupported platform, regardless of
that platform’s own `on_unsupported_param` policy. Losing these silently
is losing *content*, not a quality knob – e.g. an instrumental with none
of the caller’s words in it, with no signal that happened. See
thorwhalen/arioso#3.

### arioso.translation.check_supported_params(kwargs, config, , always_raise=('lyrics',))

Warn or raise for kwargs not declared in a platform’s `supported_affordances`.

`on_unsupported_param` was, until thorwhalen/arioso#3, only ever enforced
inside [`make_kwargs_trans()`](_autosummary/arioso.translation.html.md#arioso.translation.make_kwargs_trans) – reached solely by the REST-fallback
`generate` built by [`make_generate_func()`](_autosummary/arioso.translation.html.md#arioso.translation.make_generate_func). Every platform that ships
a custom `adapter.py` (which is all 14, as of this writing) never went
through that translator: its `Adapter.generate(..., **kwargs)` absorbed
and silently dropped anything unsupported, regardless of the config’s
declared policy. Call this once, uniformly, before dispatching to *any*
adapter – see `arioso.generate`/`arioso.generate_many`.

This only validates; it does not translate or drop keys itself. The
caller’s kwargs are passed to the adapter unchanged either way.

* **Parameters:**
  * **kwargs** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – The unified-name kwargs about to be passed to an adapter
    (must not include `prompt`).
  * **config** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – The platform’s `PLATFORM_CONFIG` dict.
  * **always_raise** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)) – Affordance names that raise unconditionally when
    unsupported, overriding the platform’s own policy.
* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### arioso.translation.make_generate_func(config)

Build a generate() callable from a platform config.

This is the fallback when no custom adapter.py is provided.
For REST API platforms, it builds the HTTP function from the config
and wraps it with parameter translation and output normalization.

* **Parameters:**
  **config** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – A PLATFORM_CONFIG dict.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)
* **Returns:**
  A callable that accepts unified affordance kwargs and returns
  a Song.

### arioso.translation.make_kwargs_trans(param_map, , on_unsupported='warn', passthrough=())

Build a kwargs translation function from a platform’s param_map.

The returned function transforms:

```default
{common_name: value, ...}  ->  {native_name: coerced_value, ...}
```

* **Parameters:**
  * **param_map** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – Dict mapping common affordance names to native config
    dicts.  Each value has keys: `native_name` (str),
    `coerce` (optional callable), `adapter_handled` (optional
    bool), `type` (optional Python class: narrows the AFFORDANCES
    type for the soft type check in `arioso.services`, e.g. `str`
    for a `continue_from` that is a clip id on that platform).
  * **on_unsupported** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What to do with params not in param_map.
    One of ‘warn’, ‘raise’, or ‘ignore’.
  * **passthrough** – Adapter-only keyword names (a config’s
    `adapter_params`) passed through untranslated and unwarned.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]
* **Returns:**
  A function that translates outer kwargs to inner kwargs.

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`arioso` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `arioso`

Generate music with AI using the `arioso` package — one Python interface over 16 music-generation backends (Suno, ElevenLabs Music, Udio, YuE, ACE-Step, MusicGen, Stable Audio, Stable Audio 2.5, Riffusion, Harmonai, Lyria, Mubert, Beatoven, Loudly, Jen). Use when the user wants to “make a song”, “generate music”, “write a song about X”, “turn this poem/text/script into a song”, “set these lyrics to music”, “text to music”, “make a theme tune”, “I need background music”, or “a royalty-free instrumental track”, “music under the narration”, “a bed for this voice-over” — or when they name a platform (Suno, ElevenLabs Music, Udio, MusicGen, Stable Audio, Riffusion, Lyria). Covers the one-line call, which five backends can actually SING lyrics you wrote (the other eleven drop them silently), the Suno customMode title/genre requirement, which backends are free versus paid, polling an async job, and writing the audio to disk.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/arioso arioso --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`arioso/data/skills/arioso`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/arioso/tree/HEAD/arioso/data/skills/arioso) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install arioso`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/arioso/tree/HEAD/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/arioso/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`arioso.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/arioso/arioso.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/arioso/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
